Once the *pārivāsika* period is completed, one should perform the *mānatva* penance for six nights. Then, within an assembly of twenty bhikṣus, the restoration from the offense (*ābṛhaṇa*) should be granted.
This matter is shameful among the assembly and brings contempt from others.
Within this context, you must not intentionally emit semen.
Are you able to refrain from doing so?
If one is able to say "yes," one must not intentionally touch the body of a woman.
"Can you not do this thing?
If you can, you should say: 'Yes.'"
"One must not speak harsh words to women.
Can you refrain from doing so?
If they can, one should say:
"Yes. "May you not praise your own body as being worthy of offerings in front of women?
Can you refrain from doing so?"
If one is able to say "yes" [to the precepts],
one must not act as a matchmaker for women.
"Is it possible for this matter not to be done?
If you can do so, you should say: "Yes."
"One must not build a private cell for oneself; the Buddha has permitted what should be done and forbidden what should not be done.
Can you refrain from doing such things?
If you can, you should say: [Yes]."
“Yes. One must not construct large dwellings; the Buddha has permitted what should be done and prohibited what should not be done.
Are you able to refrain from doing such things?
If one can say "yes" [to the truth],
one must not slander others with groundless charges.
"Is it possible for this matter not to be done?
If it is possible, you should say: 'Yes.'"
"One should not, on account of a minor cause for offense, slander another by claiming it is a great sin.
Can you refrain from doing such a thing?
If you can, you should say so."
"Yes. "Are you able not to persistently cause a schism in the Saṃgha?"
If one can say "So be it," one must not assist those who are breaking the Sangha.
"Can you refrain from doing this?
If you can, you should say: 'Yes.'"
"One should not disparage or humiliate other families.
Are you able to refrain from doing such things?
If you can, you should say: 'I can.'"
"Yes. "Can you refrain from being headstrong and difficult to instruct? "I can."
If you can say, "So be it," and if you can maintain a mind of humble submission,

delighting in compliance with instruction, then once you have received the precepts, you will obtain a complete upādhyāya, a complete ācārya, a complete community of bhikṣus, a favorable land, and a favorable place for practicing the Way— just as the aspiration of a wheel-turning monarch.
Now that you have fulfilled these requirements, you should increase your reverence for the Three Jewels—the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus;
you should train in the Three Trainings—the training in right morality, the training in right mind, and the training in right wisdom; and you should seek the three gates of liberation.
Regarding emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, one should diligently apply oneself to the three activities:
sitting in meditation, reciting the sutras, and exhorting others in various matters.

By practicing such dharmas, one opens the gate of the Deathless and attains the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, the path of the pratyekabuddha, and the path of the Buddha—just as blue lotuses, white lotuses, red lotuses, and crimson lotuses grow day by day while in the water.
You, too, shall be thus; you shall grow day by day in the Dharma of the bhikṣus.
As for the remaining precepts, your upādhyāya and ācārya will teach them to you in detail.
You have now completed receiving full ordination.
Within the Dharma of the Lion of the Śākyas, all that is wondrous and virtuous is gathered;
he has deeply entered the boundless ocean of the jewels of merit.
This vow was for a Wheel-Turning King, a Heavenly King, or a King of the Good Dharma;
you constantly sought to become a śramaṇa, yet that was not fulfilled, whereas you have now attained it.
Through diligent practice of the three karmas, the Buddha-dharma in its immeasurable varieties [is realized].
If you constantly recollect the Dharma, you will attain all unhindered wisdoms.
Like a lotus in the water, which grows day by day,
so too shall your faith increase, as will your virtue, learning, concentration, and wisdom.
The remaining precepts are those ordained by the Buddha; the Upādhyāya and the Ācārya shall instruct them.
Having completed the prostrations and circumambulations within the assembly, they may joyfully follow their respective inclinations.
This concludes the first of the seven methods for receiving full ordination (*upasampadā*). *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, Scroll 21.
The *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, Scroll Twenty-two, Part Two of the Fourth Recitation, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Puṇyatāra of North India during the Later Qin dynasty. Section Two:
The Method for the Poṣadha; the Second [Section] among the Seven Methods: The Poṣadha Method.

The Buddha was staying in Rājagṛha. At that time, the World-Honored One had not yet permitted the bhikṣus to perform the poṣadha, nor had he permitted the poṣadha-karman, nor had he permitted the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, nor had he permitted them to assemble for the session.
At that time, a non-Buddhist brahmin asked the bhikṣus:
"Do you have the uposatha, the uposatha-karman, and the assembly for reciting the Prātimokṣa?"
He replied, "I did not.
A heterodox brahmin, out of jealousy, reviled, disparaged, and reproached him, saying:
"Other śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas still have the poṣadha, the poṣadha-karman, and the assembly for reciting the Prātimokṣa.
You śramaṇas, sons of the Śākya, claim for yourselves:
'We are virtuous and of good character.'"
Yet they did not perform the *poṣadha*, the *poṣadha-karman*, or the assembly for reciting the *prātimokṣa*.
When those bhikṣus who were of few desires, contented, and practiced the *dhūta* austerities heard of this matter, they felt shame and remorse, and reported the matter in detail to the Buddha.
For this reason, the Buddha assembled the Sangha. Having assembled the Sangha, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:

"From now on, I authorize the performance of the poṣadha, the poṣadha-karman, and the assembly for reciting the Prātimokṣa. As I have established the precepts, the Prātimokṣa should be recited every half-month."
The Buddha was staying at Rājagṛha.
At that time, the Elder Mahākapphiṇa was dwelling in a forest cave near Rājagṛha. On the fifteenth day, during the uposatha, he sat in meditation alone and thought to himself:
"Should I go to the uposatha or not?"
Should one go to the *poṣadha* ritual or not?
Should one go to recite the *prātimokṣa* or not?
Should one go to the assembly for sitting together or not?
“Purity is the foremost purity.

The Buddha, knowing the thoughts in Mahākapphiṇa’s mind, immediately entered a samādhi corresponding to that state; his physical form suddenly vanished as he remained in the state of samādhi, appearing before Mahākapphiṇa’s cave. Emerging from concentration, he spoke to Mahākapphiṇa, saying:
“You have had this thought:”
"Shall I go to the uposatha, the uposatha-karma, and the assembly for the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, or shall I not go?
I am pure, accomplished in purity, and supremely pure."
"You, Mahākoṭṭhita, brahmin, you must go to the uposatha, the uposatha-kamma, and the assembly for the recitation of the Prātimokṣa. Why is this?"

"You are a great senior elder; if you do not show reverence for, do not hold in high esteem, and do not make offerings to the *poṣadha*, who then shall revere, make offerings to, and honor the *poṣadha*?"
"You go and attend the *poṣadha* ceremony.
At that time, the Buddha himself took Mahā-Kapphiṇa by the arm and led him into the assembly for the *poṣadha*.
Upon arriving at the midst of the Saṃgha, the Buddha sat in his usual place and addressed the bhikṣus:
"From now on, two types of poṣadha are permitted:
first, that of the fourteenth day;
second, that of the fifteenth day."
First, before the meal; second, after the meal.
First, during the day; second, at night.
Whether in a forest hermitage or on the outskirts of a village, from this time forth I authorize you to perform the *poṣadha* together in harmony and establish a boundary.

In this manner, the *karmavācanā* should be performed: according to how much of a harmonious Saṃgha is assembled in a single place for the *poṣadha*, they may perform the delimitation of the boundary (*sīmābandhana*) for one *krośa*, two *krośas*, or even up to ten *krośas*.
In this regard, one bhikṣu should proclaim the boundary markers of the four directions—whether they be walls, groves, trees, mountains, rocks, roads, rivers, or ponds.
At that time, one bhikṣu should announce within the Saṃgha:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu, [name], announces the boundary marks of the four directions; everything within these marks constitutes the interior of the boundary."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha perform the formal act of establishing a boundary for a single Poṣadha and communal residence within this area.
This is the motion.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"

"Monk [Name] proclaims the boundary markers of the four directions; within these markers is the interior of the boundary, wherein the Saṃgha shall perform the Uposatha together and establish a formal boundary."
"Whichever elders among you consent to this single *poṣadha* communal residence and the establishment of the boundary, remain silent; whoever does not consent, speak up.
"The Saṃgha has completed the establishment of the boundary for this single *poṣadha* communal residence. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."
The Buddha was staying in Rājagṛha.
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa left his saṃghāṭī robe on Vulture Peak Mountain and, wearing only his upper and lower robes, came to the Bamboo Grove for a minor reason.
It happened that there was heavy rain, so they were unable to return to the mountain and stayed overnight apart from their saṃghāṭī robes.
Kāśyapa said to the bhikṣus:
"Elders!..."
I left my saṃghāṭī robe on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa; wearing only my upper and lower garments, I came to the Bamboo Grove for a minor reason.
Encountering heavy rain, I was unable to return to the mountain and thus stayed overnight separated from my saṃghāṭī.
"What shall I do? The bhikṣus reported this matter in detail to the Buddha.
On account of these causes and conditions, the Buddha assembled the Saṃgha. Having assembled the Saṃgha, the Buddha asked Mahākāśyapa:
“Is it truly so? He replied,
“It is truly so.”
"World-Honored One!

The Buddha praised the precepts and the upholding of the precepts through various causes and conditions. Having finished praising the precepts and the upholding of the precepts, he addressed the bhikṣus:

"From this day forward, I authorize within the boundary established for communal residence during a single poṣadha to perform the *karmavācanā* of 'not being separated from one's robes while staying overnight.'"
It should be done in this manner: with a single mind, the Saṃgha should be assembled. Once the Saṃgha has been assembled, one bhikṣu within the assembly should announce:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

The Saṃgha shall perform the Uposatha together and dwell together; for as much of the boundary as is established for this common dwelling, excluding villages and village boundaries therein, we shall take the open space and the residences."

If the time has come for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha, out of compassion, grant its consent: let the Saṃgha perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of "not sleeping apart from one's robes" within the boundary established for communal residence during a single *poṣadha*.
This is the motion (*jñapti*).
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

The Saṃgha shall dwell together in a single poṣadha within as much of a defined boundary (sīmā) as is appropriate; therein, excluding villages and village boundaries, we shall take the open space and the dwelling places."
Within this boundary where the Saṃgha dwells together for a single *poṣadha*, we shall perform the *karmavācanā* for "staying overnight without being separated from one's robes.

Which elders here consent to performing the "staying overnight without being separated from one's robes" within this boundary where the Saṃgha dwells together for a single *poṣadha*? Those who consent, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.

"The Saṃgha has completed this single *poṣadha* within the boundary of communal residence, having performed the practice of not sleeping apart from one's robes. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."
The Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī.
At that time, the Elder Śāriputra was ill; wishing to travel for one month, he found his saṃghāṭī too heavy to carry on his journey, so he said to the bhikṣus:
"Venerable elders!..."
"I am ill and wish to travel for about a month, but my saṃghāṭī robe is too heavy for me to carry while walking. What should I do?
The bhikṣus reported this matter in detail to the Buddha.
For this reason, the Buddha assembled the Saṃgha. Having assembled the Saṃgha, the Buddha, knowing [the answer], asked Śāriputra:
"Is it true that you did so? He replied:
"It is truly so,
World-Honored One!

After the Buddha had praised the precepts and the upholding of the precepts through various causes and conditions, and having finished praising the precepts and the upholding of the precepts, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"From now on, I permit a sick or elderly bhikṣu who wishes to travel for one month to perform the *karmavācanā* for staying apart from his *saṃghāṭī* robe.

It should be performed in this manner: The community of monks should assemble with a single mind; that sick or elderly bhikṣu should rise from his seat, baring one shoulder, put on his robes, remove his leather sandals, enter the midst of the community, prostrate at the feet of the monks, kneel with palms joined, and speak as follows:
'Venerable Elders!'"
I, [Name], being either ill or old, wish to travel for one month; however, my saṃghāṭī robe is too heavy for me to carry while traveling.
I, [Name], being either ill or old, hereby request from the Saṃgha the formal act (karmavācanā) of not being separated from my saṃghāṭī robe for one month.
Venerable Saṃgha!
I, [Name], whether due to old age or illness, request that you grant me the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of not being separated from my saṃghāṭī robe for one month, out of compassion.
A second and third time, he should likewise beg.
At that time, the Saṃgha may conceal the truth as to whether they can grant it or not. If this person says, "I am ill," [the Saṃgha should grant it].
"In truth, I am not ill;
if one says, 'I am old.'"
"It is not actually old;
if one says,
'The saṃghāṭī is too heavy.'"
"If it is truly not heavy,
one should not give it to such a person.
If they say that the saṃghāṭī is too heavy due to illness or old age, and it is indeed too heavy because of actual illness or old age, then one should give it."
In this matter, one bhikṣu should announce:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This person, so-and-so, being either ill or old, wishes to travel for one month."
This person, [name], being either ill or old, requests from the Saṃgha the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of not being separated from his *saṃghāṭī* robe for one month.

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha, out of compassion, grant this person, [name], who is either ill or old, the formal act of not being separated from his *saṃghāṭī* robe for one month.
Thus it is announced.
[The motion for] the second *karmavācanā* is as follows:

"The Saṃgha grants such-and-such a person the *karmavācanā* of not being separated from the saṃghāṭī robe for one month, whether due to illness or old age. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld!"
"The same applies to the *uttarāsaṅga* and the *antarvāsaka*.
If this is done for one month, it shall likewise be so for up to nine months.
While the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"If the Saṃgha wishes to narrow or expand the boundary, they must first relinquish the original boundary.
Whether the subsequent boundary is large or small, it should be relinquished in this manner:
the Saṃgha should assemble with a single mind, and within the assembly, one bhikṣu shall announce:"
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

Herein, the Saṃgha has performed a single *poṣadha*, dwelt together in harmony, and established a boundary (*sīmā*). If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha consents, let the Saṃgha dissolve the boundary and relinquish the boundary that was established for the purpose of dwelling together in a single *poṣadha*."
Thus it is announced:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

The Saṃgha dwells together for a single poṣadha; within this place, the Saṃgha has established a boundary. Now, at this dwelling place for the single poṣadha, the Saṃgha dissolves the boundary and relinquishes the boundary."

"Whichever elders consent to the dissolution of the boundary and the relinquishing of the boundary for the single *poṣadha* at this common residence, let them remain silent; whoever does not consent, let them speak.

"The Sangha has completed the dissolution of the boundary and the relinquishing of the boundary for the single *poṣadha* at this common residence. Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."

"When monks first construct a monastery in a village where no monastery previously existed and have not yet performed the formal boundary-determination (*sīmā-bandha*), how large should that boundary be?
The Buddha said:
"The boundary of the village itself shall be the boundary of the monastery."
When the bhikṣus were in a wilderness area devoid of villages and were first constructing a monastery before the boundary had been established, at that time, how large should the boundary be?
The Buddha said:
"It shall be one krośa square."
Among these, the bhikṣus should not perform the poṣadha or the saṃgha-karmas separately.
If they perform the poṣadha or the saṃgha-karmas separately, the bhikṣus commit an offense.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"There are four ways of reciting the Prātimokṣa.
What are the four?

First, the recitation of the Prātimokṣa by an illegal separate assembly; second, an illegal harmonious assembly; third, a legal separate assembly; and fourth, a legal harmonious assembly reciting the Prātimokṣa.

If the *prātimokṣa* is recited by an illegal assembly, it is not a valid recitation; if the *prātimokṣa* is recited by a legal assembly, it is not a valid recitation; if the *prātimokṣa* is recited by an illegal assembly, it is not a valid recitation;
however, if the *prātimokṣa* is recited by a legal assembly, it constitutes a valid recitation of the *prātimokṣa*.
Furthermore, there are five ways of reciting the Prātimokṣa.
What are the five?
The Saṃgha, being of one mind, recites the introduction to the Prātimokṣa during the Poṣadha; the rest of the Saṃgha has previously heard it.

The Prātimokṣa has been recited; the Saṃgha, being in harmony, has completed the Poṣadha. With one mind, the Saṃgha has recited the introduction to the Prātimokṣa and the four pārājikas; as for the remainder, the Saṃgha has already heard it previously.

The Prātimokṣa has been recited; the Saṃgha, being in harmony, has completed the Poṣadha. With one mind, the Saṃgha has recited the introduction to the Prātimokṣa, recited the four pārājikas, and recited the thirteen saṃghāvaśeṣas; the remainder has already been heard by the Saṃgha.

The Prātimokṣa has been recited; the Saṃgha, being in harmony, has completed the Poṣadha ceremony. With one mind, the Saṃgha has recited the introduction to the Prātimokṣa, the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṃghāvaśeṣas, the two Aniyatas, and the thirty Naiḥsargika-pāyattikas; the remainder has already been heard by the Saṃgha.
The Prātimokṣa has already been explained; the Saṃgha’s harmony and the conclusion of the Poṣadha have been completed. This is the fifth detailed exposition.
"At a certain residence, at the time of the Poṣadha, the bhikṣus were young, ignorant, unskilled, and like rams."
What is meant by being inferior, ignorant, unwholesome, and like a sheep?
It is when these bhikṣus do not know the poṣadha, do not know the poṣadha-karman, do not know how to recite the Prātimokṣa, and do not know how to assemble for the session.
When these bhikṣus are residing in this dwelling place, they should not remain there at the time of the poṣadha.
If the bhikṣus remain in this dwelling place at the time of the poṣadha, none of the bhikṣus will be able to perform the poṣadha, and they will incur an offense.
"When a bhikṣu such as this takes leave of his upādhyāya and ācārya, wishing to travel abroad,
the upādhyāya and ācārya should ask:
'With whom will you go as a companion?'"
"What kind of bhikṣu travels together [with others]?
These bhikṣus spoke of the word "companion.

If a bhikṣu is merely a companion, he does not know the uposatha, he does not know the uposatha-karman, he does not know the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, and he does not know how to sit in the assembly.
The preceptors and ācāryas should be retained.
If the preceptor or ācārya is not retained, one commits a duṣkṛta offense.
If one departs despite having been retained, one commits a duṣkṛta offense.
"If a bhikṣu departs despite being detained by his upādhyāya or ācārya, at what time does he incur an offense?
The Buddha said:
"When daybreak occurs outside the boundary, he commits a duṣkṛta offense."
"There were some bhikṣus who, while observing the rains retreat at a single residence, thought beforehand:
'When such-and-such bhikṣus recite the Prātimokṣa, not a single one of those bhikṣus will be able to recite the Prātimokṣa at the time of the first uposatha.'"

The bhikṣus should send an elder bhikṣu to a nearby residence to receive the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, whether in brief or in detail; it would be excellent if someone were to receive it and return.
If these bhikṣus are not present, one should not dwell and reside there during the summer retreat.

If these bhikṣus are residing in that place for the summer retreat, all other bhikṣus shall not perform the *poṣadha* ceremony at each individual *poṣadha* gathering; if they do so, they commit an offense.

At that time, if the resident bhikṣus hear that visiting bhikṣus have arrived who are pure, with whom they may dwell together, who share the same views, who know the poṣadha, who know the poṣadha-karman, who know how to recite the Prātimokṣa, and who know how to sit in assembly;
The senior bhikṣus should go out to meet them, greet them with gentle words, take their robes and bowls for them, and show them the rooms and bedding, saying:
"Venerable ones!
These are your rooms and bedding; these are the fine staircases, the corded couches, the plain staircases, and the mats and blankets. You may settle yourselves according to the order of the seniors."

"In this matter, the resident bhikṣus should provide bathing requisites, cleansing powder, hot water, and body-unguents such as ghee and oil according to the prescribed rules; they should also prepare and provide excellent offerings of morning and afternoon meals for the following day."
If one fails to provide offerings and support, all the elder bhikṣus incur an offense.
Why is this? In the absence of a Buddha, such a person fills the Buddha’s place.
This visiting bhikṣu is able to extensively analyze both divisions of the Prātimokṣa; for this reason, he should be provided with offerings and veneration.
"In a certain residence where four bhikṣus are performing the poṣadha, those bhikṣus should assemble in one place and perform the poṣadha in detail by reciting the Prātimokṣa."
In a certain residence where three bhikṣus are present at the time of the poṣadha, they should not recite the Prātimokṣa.
These bhikṣus should assemble in one place and perform the poṣadha by means of the "threefold speech" (trivācika); it should be done in this manner.

If the Elder wishes to perform the *poṣadha*, he should rise from his seat, adjust his robe to bare one shoulder, remove his leather sandals, kneel with his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and speak as follows:
"Venerable sirs, please bear this in mind!"
Today is the Sangha’s Uposatha day, whether it be the fourteenth or the fifteenth.
Venerable sirs, know that I am pure; I maintain the unobstructed Dharma and perform the Uposatha in purity so that the assembly may be complete in its observance of the precepts.
The second [announcement]:
"Venerable sirs, remember!
Today is the Uposatha day for the Saṃgha, whether it be the fourteenth or the fifteenth day."
"Venerable sir, know that I am pure; I recall the Dharma of the unobstructed path, and I perform the *poṣadha* with purity because the assembly of precepts is complete.
Third: "Venerable sir, please bear this in mind!"
Today is the Sangha’s Uposatha day, whether it be the fourteenth or the fifteenth.
Venerable sirs, know that I am pure; I maintain the unobstructed Dharma and perform the Uposatha in purity so that the assembly may be complete in the precepts.

If a junior monk wishes to perform the *poṣadha*, he should rise from his seat, adjust his robe to bare one shoulder, remove his leather sandals, and kneel with his right knee on the ground. With both hands, he should grasp the feet of the senior monk and speak as follows:
"Venerable sir, please take heed!"
Today is the Sangha’s *poṣadha* day, whether it be the fourteenth or the fifteenth.
Venerable sirs, know that I am pure; I recall having maintained the unobstructed path of the Dharma. I perform the *poṣadha* in purity so that the assembly of precepts may be fulfilled.
The second [announcement]:
"Venerable sirs, remember!
Today is the Uposatha day of the Sangha, whether it be the fourteenth or the fifteenth."
"Venerable sir, know that I am pure; I recall the Dharma of the unobstructed path; I perform the *poṣadha* in purity because the assembly of precepts is complete. Third:
"Venerable sir, remember!"
Today is the Sangha’s day of Uposatha, whether it be the fourteenth or the fifteenth day.
Venerable sirs, know that I am pure; I recall being free from any obstructing dharma. Being pure, I shall perform the Uposatha, so that the assembly may be complete in its observance of the precepts.
"In a certain residence where two bhikṣus are performing the poṣadha, they should not recite the Prātimokṣa.
These two bhikṣus should assemble in one place and perform the poṣadha by means of the 'threefold speech' (trivācika), just as in the case of the three bhikṣus mentioned above."

"In a certain residence, when a single bhikṣu is observing the poṣadha, that bhikṣu should sweep the stūpa, sweep the poṣadha hall, and sweep the ground. Having finished sweeping, he should arrange the rope-beds in order, prepare fire-lamps, basket-lamps, wick-lamps, and prepare the counting sticks. He should then reflect thus:
'If other bhikṣus come, and the poṣadha has not yet been performed, this bhikṣu shall perform the poṣadha together with them by reciting the Prātimokṣa.'"
If they do not come, one should stand at a high place within that area and look out; if one sees any bhikṣus, one should call out to them:
"Come quickly, venerable elders!"
"Today is the *poṣadha*.
If he does not see [the assembly], he should wait until evening and return to sit in his original place, making this reflection and verbal declaration:
'Today the Saṃgha holds the *poṣadha*, whether on the fourteenth or the fifteenth day; I too shall hold the *poṣadha* today.'"
"In this manner, one bhikṣu completes the poṣadha.
While the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī, he said to the bhikṣus:
"This night has passed far too long; the Prātimokṣa should be recited."
At that time, a certain bhikṣu rose from his seat, bared one shoulder, joined his palms, and said to the Buddha:
"There are some sick bhikṣus who have not come.
The Buddha said:
"You should bring purity.
It should be brought in this manner; you should say to the bhikṣu:
'Give me your purity.'"
He replied, "I give it.
This is called attaining purity.
If one says,
"Speak of purity for me within the Saṃgha," this is called obtaining purity.
If one gives by means of bodily movement, this is called attaining purity.
If one says with the mouth,
"I give."
This is called attaining purity.
If the body does not participate and the mouth does not participate, this is called not attaining purity.
At that time, all the bhikṣus should go to the sick bhikṣu or have him brought [to them]; they must not perform the poṣadha and recite the Prātimokṣa separately from that bhikṣu.
If those bhikṣus perform the poṣadha and recite the Prātimokṣa separately, all the bhikṣus incur an offense.
When two bhikṣus reside at a single dwelling place, during the poṣadha they should neither receive purity nor grant purity to one another.

These two bhikṣus should assemble in one place and perform the *poṣadha* by means of the three-fold proclamation; this is the same as the *poṣadha* performed by the aforementioned group of three bhikṣus.
When three bhikṣus reside at a single dwelling and perform the *poṣadha*, they should neither receive purity nor grant purity.

These three bhikṣus should assemble in one place and perform the *poṣadha* by means of the "threefold speech" (*trivācika*), which is the same as the *poṣadha* performed by the aforementioned group of three bhikṣus.
When four bhikṣus reside at a single dwelling and it is time for the *poṣadha*, they should neither receive purity (*śuddhi*) nor grant purity.
These bhikṣus shall assemble in one place and perform the extensive poṣadha by reciting the Prātimokṣa.
If there are more than four, they must assemble together at the time of the poṣadha.
In this matter, the sick bhikṣu may take [the *pārisuddhi*] at his own discretion.
It should be taken in this manner: if one person takes it from one person, this is called taking the *pārisuddhi*.
If one person takes it from two, three, or four persons, this is called taking the *pārisuddhi*.
If there are as many people as remember only the names [of the precepts], this is called taking the purity [of the assembly].
If those who have taken the purity do not wish to take it, one should further grant the purity to other persons.
If one takes the words of a pure person and says:
"I am a layperson; I am a śrāmaṇera;
I am not a bhikṣu; I am a non-Buddhist;"
Not performing the formal act of suspension (*pratisāraṇīya-karman*), nor carrying out the suspension;
not removing evil and heterodoxy; suspending one so as not to dwell together with them; various forms of non-dwelling together;

those who have committed a grave offense, those who were originally laypeople, eunuchs, those who have defiled a bhikṣuṇī, those who have crossed over [to another sect], and those who have killed their father, killed their mother, or killed an arhat, or caused a schism in the Saṃgha.
If one says,
"I have shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind," they should instead be granted purification by another.
If one has accepted another's declaration of purity and yet does not depart, this is called "purity not having been reached.
If, after accepting another's declaration of purity, one says:
"I am a layperson" or "I am a śrāmaṇera";
"I am not a bhikṣu; I am an outsider.
I have not been seen to commit an offense requiring suspension, nor have I performed an act of suspension.
My evil and heterodox views have not been removed; I have been suspended and excluded from communal residence, and subjected to various forms of non-residence."

Those who have committed grave offenses: one who was originally a layperson, a eunuch, one who has defiled a bhikṣuṇī, one who has crossed over [to the other shore], one who has killed his father or mother, one who has killed an arhat, one who has caused a schism in the Saṃgha, or one who has shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind.
This is called "purity that does not reach [the goal].
If, after one has attained the purity of another, each of the eight difficulties arises and one does not depart from them, this is called "purity that does not reach [the goal]."
Furthermore, having completed the purification of another, one does not depart due to negligence, laziness, sleep, or entering meditative absorption; this is called "purification without arrival."
For one who has undertaken this purification, there are three causes and conditions for incurring an offense:
if one intentionally fails to practice, if one is negligent, or if one is lazy.
There are two causes and conditions for being without offense:
If one is asleep or has entered meditative absorption; furthermore,
having received another's declaration of purity, if one does not announce it upon arriving at the Saṃgha, this is called "arrival with purity."
If one takes another who is pure into the midst of the Saṃgha and says:
"I am a layperson; I am a śrāmaṇera;
I am not a bhikṣu; I am of a different path";
Not being seen for formal suspension, not performing formal suspension;
not removing evil and heterodoxy, formal suspension through non-cohabitation, various forms of non-cohabitation;

one who has committed a pārājika offense, a former layperson, a eunuch, one who has defiled a bhikṣuṇī, one who has gone over to another sect, one who has killed his father, one who has killed his mother, one who has killed an arhat, and one who has caused a schism in the Saṃgha.
If one says,
"I have shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind," this is called reaching purity.
Furthermore, having received another's declaration of purity, one arrives before the Saṃgha; if any of the eight obstacles arise and one does not speak [of them], this is called "arrival with purity.

Furthermore, having received another's declaration of purity, one arrives before the Saṃgha; if one intentionally does not speak, or due to negligence, laziness, sleep, or entering meditative absorption, this is called "arrival with purity."
Among the Sangha, those who have received the purity [of confession] incur an offense due to three causes:
if they intentionally fail to speak, if they are negligent, or if they are indolent.
There are two causes for which there is no offense: [the other two being]...
Whether he is asleep or in meditative absorption.

"If, at the time of the *poṣadha* in a certain residence, a monk is seized by a king, or by a thief, or by an enemy, or by a partisan of an enemy, or by one who is allied with such a partisan, the Saṃgha should send a messenger to him, saying:
'Today the Saṃgha performs the *poṣadha*. You should either come here, or grant us your purity (*śuddhi*), or go outside the boundary; we should not perform the *poṣadha* separately.'"
If that bhikṣu can come, or if he grants his purity, or if he goes outside the boundary, it is well.
If none of these is possible, the bhikṣus should not perform the poṣadha separately.
"If there is a separate *poṣadha*, all the bhikṣus commit an offense.
The Buddha said to the bhikṣus:
"The Saṃgha must not engage in such a formal act as this."
"At this time, the Elder Śīva should be granted the *parivāsa* penance.
A certain bhikṣu rose from his seat, bared one shoulder, removed his leather sandals, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha,
saying, "Venerable Sir!"
"There are some sick bhikṣus who have not come; I have granted them purity.
The Buddha said, "Those bhikṣus are themselves pure; therefore, I have granted them purity."
Now this bhikṣu should come to convey his consent (*chanda*).
He should convey it in this manner:
he should speak to that bhikṣu as follows:
"Come with the consent.
Or if one says:
"Give the consent."
This is called "obtaining the *chanda*.
If one says, "On my behalf,
speak the *chanda* to the Saṃgha," [it is likewise].
This is called obtaining what one desires.
If one gives by means of bodily movement, this is called obtaining what one desires.
Or if one says with the mouth:
"To give" is called obtaining consent.
If one does not give with the body nor give with speech, this is called not obtaining consent.
All these bhikṣus should perform the *karmavācanā* (formal ritual act) either by going to the side of the sick bhikṣu or by bringing him there.
The bhikṣus must not perform the *karmavācanā* separately; if they perform it separately, all the bhikṣus incur an offense.
If one person takes another person’s desire, this is called "obtaining desire.
If one person takes [the desire of] two, three, or four people, this is called "obtaining desire.
According to however many people whose names are remembered, that is called "obtaining desire."
If one takes [an offering] from a person who desires to give it but does not wish to take it back, one should give it to another person.
If the person from whom it was taken says:
"I am a layperson" or "I am a śrāmaṇera";
"I am not a bhikṣu; I belong to another path;
I have not been seen to commit an offense, nor have I performed an act of formal suspension;
my evil and heterodox views have not been removed; I have been suspended and am no longer in communal residence; I am excluded from various forms of communal life."

Those who have committed offenses against the border [of the Sangha], those who were originally laypeople, eunuchs, those who have defiled a bhikṣuṇī, those who have crossed over [to another sect], those who have killed their father or mother, those who have killed an arhat, those who have caused a schism in the Saṃgha, and those who have shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind.
"One should further give one's consent (*chanda*) to another.
If, having taken another's consent, one does not depart, this is called 'the consent not having arrived.
If the person who took the consent says:"
"I am a layperson; I am a śrāmaṇera;
I am not a bhikṣu; I am a follower of another path;
I have not been seen to commit an offense; I have not been subjected to the formal act of suspension."
Not removing evil and heterodoxy; being expelled and not living together; various forms of non-residence;

one who has committed a pārājika offense while originally a layperson; a eunuch; one who has defiled a bhikṣuṇī; one who has gone over to another sect; one who has killed his father or mother; one who has killed an arhat; one who has caused a schism in the Saṃgha; or one who, with malicious intent, has shed the blood of a Buddha.
This is called "not reaching the desire.
If one has already taken up another's desire, yet fails to reach it because any one of the eight difficulties arises, this is called "not reaching the desire."
If one has accepted another's invitation but does not go because of negligence, laziness, sleep, or entering meditative absorption, this is called "not reaching the destination through desire.
There are three causes and conditions by which one incurs an offense for having accepted another's invitation:
if one intentionally does not go, or if one is negligent, or if one is lazy.
There are two circumstances where there is no offense:
if one is asleep or if one has entered meditative concentration.
Furthermore, having received another's consent (*chanda*), if one goes into the midst of the Saṃgha without announcing it, this is called "consent not announced."
Having taken another's consent, he goes before the Saṃgha and says:
"I am a layperson; I am a śrāmaṇera;
I am not a bhikṣu; I am of another path."
Not being seen [for] the formal act of suspension (pratikṣepaṇīya-karman), nor performing the formal act of suspension;
not removing evil and heterodoxy; the formal act of suspension and non-residence together; various forms of non-residence together;

one who has committed a pārājika offense, one who was originally a layperson, a eunuch, one who has defiled a bhikṣuṇī, one who has gone over to another sect, one who has killed his father, one who has killed his mother, one who has killed an arhat, one who has caused a schism in the Saṃgha, or one who with an evil mind has shed the blood of a Buddha.
This is called "having arrived with the intention.

Furthermore, having taken up the intention of another and subsequently arrived among the Saṃgha, one does not speak because one or another of the eight difficulties has arisen; this is called "having arrived with the intention."

Furthermore, having finished conveying another's *chanda* (consent) to the Saṃgha, if one intentionally fails to announce it, or if one is negligent, or lazy, or asleep, or has entered meditative absorption (*samādhi*), this is called "the arrival of the *chanda*."
Among these, a person who indulges in sensual desires incurs an offense due to three causes and conditions:
if they intentionally fail to speak, if they are negligent, or if they are lazy.
There are two causes and conditions by which there is no offense:
Whether he is asleep or in meditative absorption.

"In a certain residence, while the Saṃgha was performing a formal act (*kamma*), a bhikkhu was seized by a king, or by a thief, or by an enemy, or by the party of an enemy, or by the party of that party."
The Saṃgha should send a messenger to say to him:

"Today the Saṃgha is performing a formal act (*karmavācanā*). Whether you are able to come, or whether you grant your consent (*chanda*), or whether you go outside the boundary, we should not perform the formal act separately."
"If that bhikṣu returns, or grants his consent (*chanda*), or goes outside the boundary—it is well.
If none of these is possible, the bhikṣus should not perform the *karmavācanā* separately."
"If one performs the *karmavācanā* separately, all the bhikṣus incur an offense.
While the Buddha was staying in Rājagṛha, at that time the Elder Śreṇika’s mind became deranged and inverted.
This elder sometimes came for the *poṣadha* ceremony and sometimes did not;
sometimes he came for the *saṃgha-karman* and sometimes did not.
The bhikṣus harbored doubts and felt regret, and they reported this matter in detail to the Buddha.
For this reason, the Buddha assembled the Saṃgha. Having assembled the Saṃgha, the Buddha, knowing [the answer], asked Śreṣṭha:
"Is it true that you did so?
He replied: [Yes].
"It is truly so,
World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to the bhikṣus:
“Gather together and perform the *unmattaka-karman* (the ritual for one who is insane) against Śikṣācāra.
If there are other monks who are likewise insane, the Saṃgha should likewise perform the *karman* for them.
It should be done in this manner: with a single mind, assemble the Saṃgha, and one monk shall proclaim:”
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This Śikṣyaka is deranged and his mind is inverted; sometimes he comes to the poṣadha, and sometimes he does not;
sometimes he comes to the saṃgha’s karmavācanā, and sometimes he does not; thus the bhikṣus have doubts and feel regret."

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent and listen: the Saṃgha shall perform the *unmattaka-karman* (the rite for one who is insane) for Śreṣṭha; whether Śreṣṭha is present or absent, the Saṃgha shall perform the *poṣadha* and all other *karman* as it sees fit.
Thus it is announced.
The motion and one subsequent proclamation (*jñapti-dvitīya-karman*) are as follows:
"The Saṃgha has completed the *śīlavipanna-unmatta-karman*. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be held thus!"
If the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for insanity has not yet been performed, one should not perform the *poṣadha* or the monastic formal acts separately.
If the formal act for insanity has already been performed, whether separately or together with the community, the Saṃgha may perform the *poṣadha* and monastic formal acts as it sees fit.
"At a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, all the bhikṣus were possessed of offenses, yet they did not know how to eliminate those offenses.
There was a visiting bhikṣu who was pure and shared the same views as the residents."
If that visiting bhikṣu recognizes among the resident bhikṣus one who is virtuous and of good character, he should ask him:
"Venerable sir!
If a bhikṣu performs such and such an act, what offense will he incur?"
He replied:
"The bhikṣu committed such-and-such an act and incurred such-and-such an offense. He said:
"Venerable one!
Do you yourself remember having done such and such a thing?
He replied:
"I recall that it is not only I who have incurred this offense; the entire Saṃgha has also incurred this offense.
The visiting bhikṣu said:
"Venerable sir!"
"What benefit do you derive from speaking against the entire Saṃgha?
Why do you not repent for your offense according to the Dharma?
If the resident bhikṣu accepts the words of the visiting bhikṣu, he shall repent for that offense according to the Dharma.
When the other bhikṣus see this bhikṣu repenting, they too should likewise repent according to the Dharma. It would be well if they do so.
If they do not, they should know that if it is beneficial, they should proceed with the formal act of *ukkhepanīyakamma*; if it is not beneficial, they should not insist on performing the act.

"If there is a residence where, at the time of the *poṣadha*, a bhikṣu remembers having committed an offense, that bhikṣu should confess that offense according to the Dharma in the presence of another bhikṣu."
When this has been completed, one should perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; one must not obstruct the *poṣadha* or the recitation of the *Prātimokṣa*.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, there is a bhikṣu who has a doubt regarding a transgression. That bhikṣu should say to the other bhikṣus:
'Venerable sirs!'"
"I have one matter of doubt; I shall ask about this matter later.
Having made such a declaration, one should perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; one must not break the *poṣadha*.
"If there is a residence where the *poṣadha* is observed and the *prātimokṣa* is recited, and a bhikṣu remembers an offense and wishes to confess it, that bhikṣu should single-mindedly reflect:
'I shall later confess this offense according to the Dharma.'"
Having performed these rites, one should conduct the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; one must not break the *poṣadha*.
If, while the *Prātimokṣa* is being recited, a monk has doubt regarding a single offense, that monk should mindfully reflect to himself:
"I shall inquire about this offense later."
When this has been completed, one should perform the *poṣadha* by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*; one must not break the *poṣadha* to recite the *Prātimokṣa*.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, the entire community of monks (*bhikṣusaṃgha*) has committed an offense and is aware of that offense. However, they are unable to obtain a visiting monk who is pure, with whom they may dwell together and share the same view regarding that offense, so as to perform the confession according to the Dharma.

Those monks should dispatch one monk [with these instructions]: 'Go quickly to a nearby residence; once you have finished confessing that offense there according to the Dharma, return, and we shall confess that offense according to the Dharma in your presence.'"
If that bhikṣu is able to accomplish this matter well, it is fine; if he is not able to accomplish it, the Saṃgha should appoint one bhikṣu to announce:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."

We, the resident monks of this dwelling, have committed offenses and recognize those offenses; yet we are unable to attain purity, nor can we dwell together with visiting bhikṣus who share the same view regarding these offenses so that we may repent according to the Dharma, nor can we manage to dispatch the resident bhikṣus to a nearby dwelling so that they may quickly go there, repent for these offenses according to the Dharma, and then return.
The monks shall confess this offense according to the Dharma before this monk.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent; the Saṃgha shall later confess this offense according to the Dharma.
Having made this announcement in this manner, once it has been completed, one should perform the *poṣadha* by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*; one must not break the *poṣadha* by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*.
"At a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, if all the bhikṣus have a doubt regarding a single matter, one bhikṣu therein should announce as follows:
'Venerable Saṃgha, listen!'"
Regarding this matter, all the bhikṣus dwelling here have a doubt concerning one specific point.
If the Saṃgha deems it the right time and grants its permission, the Saṃgha shall later inquire into this matter.
Thus is the formal motion (jñapti).
"Having performed these actions, one should conduct the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; one must not disrupt the *poṣadha*.
At a certain residence, when it was time for the *poṣadha*, four or more resident monks assembled at the place of the *poṣadha* and conducted the *poṣadha* by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*."
If monks from another residence come who are pure, with whom one may dwell together, and who share the same views in great number, these monks should recite the Prātimokṣa once again.
When this has been completed, the former bhikṣus are without fault.

If the bhikṣus have finished the poṣadha and the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, and while no one has yet risen from their seats or departed, other bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, dwell together with them, and share the same views in great numbers, then these latter bhikṣus should perform the recitation again.
When this has been completed, the original bhikṣus are without fault.

If, after the bhikṣus have finished the poṣadha and the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, some have already left while others have not yet left, and more bhikṣus arrive from another location who are pure, dwell together with them, and share the same views, then these bhikṣus should perform the recitation again.
When this has been completed, the original bhikṣus are without fault.

If, after these bhikṣus have finished the poṣadha and the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, they have all risen from their seats but have not yet departed, and other bhikṣus residing elsewhere arrive who are pure, living together with them, and share the same views in great numbers, the bhikṣus should perform the recitation again.
When this has been performed, the previous monks are likewise without fault.
At a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, four or more resident monks assemble at the place of the *poṣadha*, intending to perform the *poṣadha* by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*.

Furthermore, if there are monks coming from another location who are pure, with whom one dwells together, and whose views are largely the same, these monks should be permitted to follow the sequence [of the assembly].

If the *poṣadha* has been completed by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*, and all those originally seated have not yet departed, and there are monks coming from another location who are pure, with whom one dwells together, and whose views are largely the same, these visiting monks should perform the *poṣadha* by means of the "threefold formula" (*trivācika*) before the resident monks.

If the bhikṣus have completed the poṣadha by reciting the Prātimokṣa, and some have already left while others have not yet left, and there arrive other bhikṣus from another location who are pure, living together, and hold the same views, but are few in number, then they should perform the poṣadha by means of a threefold verbal proclamation in the presence of those bhikṣus who have not yet left.

If the bhikṣus have finished the poṣadha ceremony and the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, and while they have all risen but not yet departed, other bhikṣus arrive from another location who are pure, dwell together with them, and share the same views, though they are few in number—if these bhikṣus can attain a common mind, it would be well for them to perform the poṣadha again in full detail and recite the Prātimokṣa.
If they cannot achieve unanimity, they should go outside the boundary and perform the *poṣadha* by means of the threefold proclamation.
If, while the resident bhikṣus are performing the *poṣadha* and reciting the *Prātimokṣa*, other resident bhikṣus arrive—whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
"If there are more, or if they are equal in number, it should be explained further; if there are fewer, one should listen to the sequence.
'When an elder bhikṣu is reciting the Prātimokṣa, guest bhikṣus arrive—whether they are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.'"
If they are more numerous, it should be explained further; if they are equal or fewer, one should listen to the sequence.

When an elder bhikṣu is reciting the Prātimokṣa during the poṣadha ceremony, other elder bhikṣus—whether guests or residents—may arrive together with him, whether they are more numerous, equal, or fewer.
"If there are more, or an equal number, it should be explained further; if there are fewer, one should listen in sequence.
"If, while resident bhikṣus are performing the poṣadha and reciting the Prātimokṣa, other guest bhikṣus arrive—whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer—"
"If there are more [newcomers], it should be explained further; if they are equal or fewer, one should listen to the sequence.
'If, while visiting bhikṣus are performing the poṣadha and reciting the Prātimokṣa, resident bhikṣus arrive—whether they are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.'"
If they are numerous or equal in number, it should be explained further; if they are few, one should listen to the sequence.
When visiting bhikṣus are performing the poṣadha and reciting the Prātimokṣa, resident bhikṣus may arrive together with them, whether they are numerous, equal, or few.
If they are equal in number, it should be explained further; if they are fewer, one should listen to the sequence.

"When resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus perform the poṣadha and recite the Prātimokṣa together, the resident bhikṣus and the visiting bhikṣus may arrive together, whether they are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer."
If they are equal in number, it should be explained further; if they are fewer, one should listen to the sequence.
When resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*, the resident bhikṣus may arrive who are either more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If they are equal in number, it should be explained further; if they are fewer, one should listen to the sequence.
When an established bhikṣu and a visiting bhikṣu are together performing the poṣadha and reciting the Prātimokṣa, a visiting bhikṣu arrives—whether he is more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If there are many, they should speak further; if there are few, they should listen to the sequence.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, four or more resident monks gathered at the place of assembly, intending to perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*."
Furthermore, there may come monks from other places who are pure, with whom one dwells together, and who share the same views; they think to themselves:
"In this place, four or more resident monks have assembled at the *poṣadha* site, intending to perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*."
"We should perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.
With the perception of purity, the perception of discipline (*vinaya*), and the perception of being separate from those who are united, they performed the *poṣadha* and recited the *Prātimokṣa*.

Furthermore, suppose other bhikṣus from another location arrive, who are pure, dwell together with them, share the same views, and are numerous; they should speak further [of the confession], yet the previous bhikṣus incur an offense.
Those bhikṣus, perceiving purity, perceiving the *vinaya*, being separate yet acting as one, and having a separate perception, complete the *poṣadha* by reciting the *prātimokṣa*.

If all those seated have neither risen nor departed; or if some have risen and departed while others have not yet risen or departed; or if all have risen but not yet departed, and another bhikṣu arrives from elsewhere who is pure, dwells together with them, and shares the same views in great number, that bhikṣu should speak further [of the offense], and the former bhikṣus incur guilt.
"In a certain residence, when it is time for the *poṣadha*, four or more resident monks have gathered at the *poṣadha* hall, wishing to perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.
Furthermore, suppose monks from another location arrive, who are pure, dwell together with them, and share the same views, and they think:
"If four or more resident monks have gathered at this place for the *poṣadha* intending to recite the *Prātimokṣa*, we should not perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa* here."

If these bhikṣus, with minds full of regret, perform the poṣadha and recite the Prātimokṣa while harboring individual or differing views, and subsequently other bhikṣus arrive from elsewhere who are pure, dwell together, and share the same views in great numbers, those latter bhikṣus should perform the recitation again; the former bhikṣus incur an offense.

If the bhikṣus, with minds full of regret, perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa* while perceiving some as separate and others as not separate, and when all those seated have neither risen nor departed, yet some have risen and departed while others have neither risen nor departed.

If all have arisen but not yet departed, and another bhikṣu arrives from elsewhere who is pure, dwells together with them, and shares the same views in great number, those bhikṣus should speak further; the former bhikṣus incur an offense.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, four or more resident monks gathered at the place of assembly, intending to perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.
Furthermore, there were bhikṣus coming from other places who were pure, living together, and held the same views in great numbers. These bhikṣus had this thought:
"Should we, or should we not, perform the uposatha and recite the Prātimokṣa here?"

If, while harboring doubts regarding whether one is pure or impure, or having perceptions of difference or sameness, one performs the *poṣadha* and recites the *Prātimokṣa*, and subsequently other monks arrive at that place who are pure, dwell together, and share the same views in great number, those monks should perform the recitation again; the former monks incur an offense.

If the bhikṣus, while harboring doubts as to whether they are pure or impure, or having different perceptions regarding their status, have completed the *poṣadha* by reciting the *prātimokṣa*, and while some members of the assembly have not yet risen or departed, some have risen and departed while others have not, and some have all risen but not yet departed, another bhikṣu arrives from a different location who is pure, dwells with them, and shares the same views, and this group is numerous—then these bhikṣus should perform the recitation again, and the former bhikṣus incur an offense.
"At a certain residence, when it was time for the *poṣadha*, four or more senior monks had gathered at the *poṣadha* hall, intending to perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.

Furthermore, suppose there are many bhikṣus from another location who have arrived, who are pure, living together, and sharing the same views. When the resident bhikṣus hear that many bhikṣus from another location have arrived—pure, living together, and sharing the same views—they think to themselves upon hearing this:
"There are many bhikṣus from another location who have arrived, who are pure, living together, and sharing the same views; this constitutes a dissolution, an abandonment, and a separation."
"I have no need for these bhikṣus; it is because I desire to bring about a schism in the Saṃgha.
Holding a different perception regarding those who are actually different, he performs the poṣadha and recites the Prātimokṣa.

Furthermore, if other bhikṣus come from elsewhere who are pure, with whom one may dwell together and who share the same views in great numbers, those bhikṣus should speak further [to the original group]. The former bhikṣus incur a sthūlātyaya offense because they have nearly caused a schism in the Saṃgha.
These bhikṣus, desiring and delighting in the schism of the Saṃgha, entertain the notion of division while performing the *poṣadha* and reciting the *Prātimokṣa*.
When they have finished, if all those seated have neither risen nor departed; or some have risen and departed while others have not risen or departed; or all have risen but not yet departed.

Furthermore, if other bhikṣus arrive from elsewhere who are pure, with whom he dwells together and who share the same views in great numbers, those bhikṣus should speak further [against him]; the former bhikṣu incurs a sthūlātyaya offense because he is close to causing a schism in the Saṃgha.
If, while the resident bhikṣus are reciting the Prātimokṣa, other resident bhikṣus arrive— whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer—
if they are more numerous or equal, the recitation should be repeated.

If resident bhikṣus are reciting the Prātimokṣa when visiting bhikṣus arrive—whether they are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer—if they are more numerous or equal, the recitation should be performed again.
When the resident bhikṣus are reciting the Prātimokṣa, the resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus arrive together, whether they are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If there are more [resident bhikṣus] or an equal number, it should be explained further.
When a guest bhikṣu is reciting the Prātimokṣa, other guest bhikṣus arrive—whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If they are numerous or equal, it should be explained further:
"When a visiting bhikṣu is reciting the Prātimokṣa, resident bhikṣus arrive—whether they are numerous, equal, or few."
If they are numerous or equal, it should be explained further:
when visiting bhikṣus recite the Prātimokṣa, resident bhikṣus may arrive together with them— whether they are numerous, equal, or few.
If they are numerous, equal, or fewer, it should be explained further.
When resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus recite the Prātimokṣa together, the resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus may arrive together, whether they are numerous, equal, or few.
If they are numerous or equal in number, it should be explained further:
"When the resident bhikṣus and the visiting bhikṣus are reciting the Prātimokṣa together, the resident bhikṣus arrive—whether they are numerous, equal, or few."
If they are numerous or equal in number, it should be explained further:
"When the resident bhikṣus and the visiting bhikṣus are reciting the Prātimokṣa together, the visiting bhikṣus arrive—whether they are numerous, equal, or few."
If they are numerous or equal, it should be stated further:

"The resident bhikṣus have many on the fourteenth-day *poṣadha*, while the guest bhikṣus have few on the fifteenth-day *poṣadha*. The guest bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus; on this day, the *poṣadha* should be performed."

If the resident bhikṣus are fourteen days behind while the visiting bhikṣus are fifteen days ahead, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus; on that day, the poṣadha should not be performed.

If the resident bhikṣus are numerous on the fifteenth day and the visiting bhikṣus are few on the first day, the visiting bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus and perform the poṣadha on that day.

If the resident bhikṣus are few on the fifteenth day and the visiting bhikṣus are numerous on the first day, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus and go outside the boundary to perform the poṣadha.

If the visiting bhikṣus have fourteen days remaining and the resident bhikṣus have fifteen days remaining, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus and perform the uposatha on that day.

If the visiting bhikṣus have fourteen days remaining and the resident bhikṣus have fifteen days remaining, the visiting bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus; they should not perform the uposatha on that day.
If there are many visiting bhikṣus on the fifteenth day and few resident bhikṣus on the first day, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus and perform the uposatha again on that day.

If the visiting bhikṣus are few on the fifteenth day and the resident bhikṣus are many on the first day, the visiting bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus in going outside the boundary to perform the *poṣadha*.

In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, the resident bhikṣus hear the signs of visiting bhikṣus—the sound of footsteps, the sound of staffs, the sound of leather sandals, or the voices of strangers—and yet these bhikṣus do not seek them out or look for them, but instead proceed to perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; the resident bhikṣus incur an offense.
If one seeks [to invite] but they do not respond, yet the *poṣadha* is performed and the *prātimokṣa* is recited, the resident bhikṣus incur an offense.
If one seeks [to invite] but cannot find them, yet proceeds with doubt, performs the *poṣadha*, and recites the *prātimokṣa*, the resident bhikṣus incur an offense.
If one seeks [a visiting monk] but cannot find him, there is no cause for doubt; one may perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*, and thus the resident monks are free from offense.
If one finds a visiting monk, one should perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa* with a single-minded and joyful heart; thus the resident monks are free from offense.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, the visiting monks hear the signs of the resident monks and the circumstances of the resident monks—such as the sound of a door bolt, the sound of a chisel, the sound of an axe, or the sound of reciting the scriptures. If these visiting monks do not seek out or inquire [about them], but instead perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*, the visiting monks incur an offense."
If one seeks [to invite] those who do not respond, yet the *poṣadha* is performed and the *prātimokṣa* is recited, the visiting *bhikṣus* incur an offense.

If one seeks [to invite them] but is unable to find them, and the *poṣadha* is performed and the *prātimokṣa* is recited out of doubt [regarding their presence], the visiting *bhikṣus* incur an offense.
If one seeks [a resident bhikṣu] but cannot find him, there is no doubt that the *poṣadha* may be performed by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*; the visiting bhikṣus are without fault.
If one seeks and finds resident bhikṣus, they should perform the *poṣadha* with a single-minded joy and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; the visiting bhikṣus are without fault.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, an established monk sees the signs of an incoming monk or the circumstances of an incoming monk; yet, if he does not recognize [the visitor's] robes and bowl, or his staff, or his oil-skin bag, leather sandals, or needle-case—if these monks do not seek [to identify themselves], and the *poṣadha* for the recitation of the *Prātimokṣa* is performed, the established monk incurs an offense."
If one seeks [to invite] but they do not respond, yet the *poṣadha* is performed and the *prātimokṣa* is recited, the resident bhikṣus incur an offense.
If one seeks [to invite] but cannot find them, yet proceeds with doubt, performing the *poṣadha* and reciting the *prātimokṣa*, the resident bhikṣus incur an offense.
If one seeks [the assembly] but cannot find it, and there is no doubt, one may perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; in this way, the senior bhikṣu incurs no offense.
If one finds [the assembly] and attains a single-minded state of joy, one should perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*; in this way, the senior bhikṣu incurs no offense.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *poṣadha*, when visiting monks see signs of resident monks—such as the ground having been freshly swept and watered, or beds having been arranged in order—if those visiting monks do not seek out or inquire [about the residents], yet proceed to perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*, the visiting monks incur an offense."
If one searches for [a guest monk] and does not call him, yet holds the *poṣadha* and recites the *Prātimokṣa*, the visiting monk incurs an offense.
If one searches for him but cannot find him, yet, out of doubt, holds the *poṣadha* and recites the *Prātimokṣa*, the visiting monk incurs an offense.
If one searches for them and cannot find them, there is no cause for doubt; if the *poṣadha* is performed and the *prātimokṣa* is recited, the visiting bhikṣus are without offense.
If they are found and one performs the *poṣadha* and recites the *prātimokṣa* with a single-minded joy, the visiting bhikṣus are without offense.

"One should not go during the *poṣadha* ceremony if there is a monk at this residence and a monk at that residence; if there is a monk at that residence but none at this one; if there is neither a monk at that residence nor at this one; or if the monks between those two places do not live together."

One should not go during the *poṣadha* ceremony if there is a monk residing at one's own place, but no monk resides at the other; or if no monk resides at the other; or if no monk resides at either place; or if monks do not dwell together in the space between those two places.

"One should not go at the time of the *poṣadha* if: there is a monk here who has no dwelling; that monk over there has no dwelling; that monk over there has both a dwelling and no dwelling; that person over there is not a monk and has a dwelling; that person over there is not a monk and has no dwelling; that person over there is not a monk and has both a dwelling and no dwelling; or if that monk over there has a dwelling, yet the monks between them do not dwell together."

"One should not go at the time of the *poṣadha* if: there is a monk here who has a residence or does not have a residence; there is a monk there who has a residence or does not have a residence; there is one who is not a monk there who has a residence; there is one who is not a monk there who does not have a residence; there is one who is not a monk there who both has and does not have a residence; there is a monk there who has a residence; there is a monk there who does not have a residence; or if the monks between those two places do not dwell together."

"One should not go during the *poṣadha* [if one thinks]: 'This place has monks who are not monks; that place has non-monks as residents; that place has non-monks who are not residents; that place has non-monks both as residents and non-residents; that monk has a residence; that monk has no residence; that monk has both a residence and no residence; the monks in between do not dwell together.'"

"One should not go at the time of the *poṣadha* [if one thinks]: 'This monk has no dwelling place; that non-monk has no dwelling place; that non-monk has both a dwelling place and no dwelling place; that monk has a dwelling place; that monk has no dwelling place; that monk has both a dwelling place and no dwelling place; that non-monk has a dwelling place; and the monks therein do not dwell together.'"

"One should not go during the *poṣadha* [if one thinks]: 'This monk is not a monk; he has a dwelling place or does not have a dwelling place; that one is not a monk; he has a dwelling place or does not have a dwelling place; this monk has a dwelling place; this monk does not have a dwelling place; this monk has a dwelling place or does not have a dwelling place; that one is not a monk; he has a dwelling place or does not have a dwelling place; the monks there do not live in communion.'"

"One should not go at the time of the *poṣadha* if: there is a monk here who has a residence; that monk has a residence; that monk has no residence; that monk both has and does not have a residence; that non-monk has a residence; that non-monk has no residence; that non-monk both has and does not have a residence; or if the monks between them do not dwell together—except in the case of monastic business or urgent matters."

One should not go during the *poṣadha* ceremony if: there is a monk here who has no dwelling place; that monk over there has no dwelling place; that monk over there has both a dwelling place and no dwelling place; that person over there is not a monk but has a dwelling place; that person over there is not a monk and has no dwelling place; that person over there is not a monk and has both a dwelling place and no dwelling place; or if that monk over there has a dwelling place but the monks between them do not live together—unless it be for a matter of the Saṃgha or an urgent matter.

One should not go during the *poṣadha* ceremony if: there is a monk here who has a residence or no residence; that monk has a residence or no residence; that person is not a monk and has a residence; that person is not a monk and has no residence; that person is not a monk and has both a residence and no residence; that monk has a residence; or that monk has no residence—and if the monks between them do not live in communal harmony—except in the case of monastic business or urgent matters.

"One should not go at the time of the *poṣadha* if: there is a bhikṣu who is not a bhikṣu and has a residence; he is not a bhikṣu and has no residence; he is not a bhikṣu and both has and has no residence; there is a bhikṣu who has a residence; there is a bhikṣu who has no residence; there is a bhikṣu who both has and has no residence; or if the bhikṣus in between do not dwell together—except in the case of monastic business or urgent matters."

"One should not go during the *poṣadha* [if one thinks]: 'This place has bhikṣus who are not bhikṣus and have no residence; that place has non-bhikṣus with no residence; that place has non-bhikṣus with both residence and no residence; that bhikṣu has a residence; that bhikṣu has no residence; that bhikṣu has both residence and no residence; that non-bhikṣu has a residence. In such cases, the bhikṣus between them do not dwell together, except for matters concerning the Saṃgha or urgent business."

"One should not go at the time of the *poṣadha* if there is a monk who is not a monk, whether he has a dwelling or no dwelling; if that other person is not a monk, whether he has a dwelling or no dwelling; if that monk has a dwelling; if that monk has no dwelling; if that monk has both a dwelling and no dwelling; if that other person has a dwelling; or if that other person has no dwelling—and if the monks in between do not live in common with one another, except for matters concerning the Saṃgha or urgent business."

"At the time of the *poṣadha*, one should go [to the assembly] where there are monks with a residence, where there are monks with a residence, where there are monks without a residence, where there are monks both with and without a residence, and where those monks are pure and dwell together."

The Buddha said:
"One should not recite the Prātimokṣa during the poṣadha in the presence of laypeople."

One should not perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa* in the presence of those who are ineligible: before a *śrāmaṇera*, a non-Bhikṣu, a follower of another path, one who has not been seen [to have committed an offense], one for whom the formal act of suspension (*pravāsanīya-karman*) has not been performed, one whose evil and heterodox views have not been relinquished, one who does not live in communion (*asaṃvāsika*), one who lives in various forms of non-communion, one who has committed a pārājika offense, one who was originally a layperson, a eunuch, one who has defiled a Bhikṣuṇī, a renegade, one who has killed his father or mother, one who has killed an Arhat, one who has caused a schism in the Saṃgha, or one who has shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind. In all such cases, one should not perform the *poṣadha* in their presence and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.
Once all prior matters have been settled, the Saṃgha should perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.
If there is one for whom the *saṃmukhavinaya* should be granted, it has been granted; if there is one for whom the *smṛtivinaya* should be granted, it has been granted;
if there is one for whom the *amūḍhavinaya* should be granted, it has been granted; if there is one for whom the *pratijñākāraka-vinaya* should be granted, it has been granted. If...

or if it is appropriate to grant the *tajjanīya* (reprimand) kamma, having granted it; or if it is appropriate to grant the *niyassa* (dependence) kamma, having granted it;
or if it is appropriate to grant the *pabbājaniya* (banishment) kamma, having granted it; or if it is appropriate to grant the *paṭisāraṇīya* (requiring reconciliation) kamma, having granted it.
If the *tajjaniya-kamma* of suspension for not seeing an offense has been completed; if the *niyassa-kamma* of suspension for not relinquishing evil views has been completed;
if the *pārivāsika-kamma* of probation has been completed;
or if the *mānatta*, *mūlāyapaṭikassana*, and *abbhāna-kamma* of penance and restoration from guilt have been completed, the Saṃgha should perform the *poṣadha* and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.
If a bhikṣu has previously received [an invitation to] purity, he should not participate in the *poṣadha* by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*.

If the Saṃgha has not yet risen from such [a state], and the day for the *poṣadha* has not yet arrived, one should not perform the *poṣadha* by reciting the *Prātimokṣa*, except in the case where a schismatic Saṃgha has returned to harmony and is listening to the *poṣadha* with a single mind.

3. The Method of *Pravāraṇā* (Invitation to Criticism). This is the third of the seven methods.
When the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī, during the summer retreat (*varṣā*), the bhikṣus first established this restriction:
"Venerable sirs!..."
"We shall not converse with one another, nor exchange greetings.
Having established this rule, those bhikṣus entered the summer retreat in one place, first instituting the following practice:

whenever anyone returned from their first alms-round, they would spread out a separate sitting mat, set out water for washing the feet, a foot-stool, and a towel for wiping the feet, as well as a vessel for pure water and a vessel for constant use.
If there is leftover food, place it in a clean vessel, cover it, and set it aside; those whose portions are insufficient shall eat this surplus food.
If there are further mendicants who arrive later and their portions are insufficient, they may take and eat from it as well.
If there is any remainder, place it on ground where no grass grows, or in water where there are no insects.

These elders shall thoroughly wash and scrub their food vessels and set them aside in one place. They shall sit alone upon their seats, and likewise set aside the foot-washing stools, foot-cloths, pure-water jars, and constant-use jars in a secluded spot. They shall sweep and sprinkle the dining hall.
Having finished sweeping, he entered the room and sat in meditation.
