When these elders rose first from meditation in the late afternoon, they would see that the water jar for rinsing, the water jar for constant use, or the foot-washing basin were empty and without water; they would then carry them to the water source, and if they could do so alone, they would bring them back and set them aside.

If he is unable to bring it himself, he should beckon other bhikṣus with his hand to lift it together and bring it back to its original place; he should neither converse with them nor exchange greetings.
It is the constant law of all Buddhas to hold two great assemblies during the final months of spring and the final month of summer.
When it is time for the *varṣā* retreat at the end of spring, bhikṣus from various regions and kingdoms come to hear the Buddha preach the Dharma.
He thought to himself:
"This Dharma is the joy of the summer retreat.
This was the first great assembly.
At the end of the summer months, having completed the *varṣā* retreat and finished the *pravāraṇā* ceremony and the making of robes, he took his robe and bowl and went to where the Buddha was.
He thought to himself:
"I have not seen the Buddha for a long time; I have not seen the Sugata for a long time."
This was the second great assembly.

Those bhikṣus who had resided there for the summer retreat, having completed their *pravāraṇā* and finished making their robes, took up their robes and bowls and went to where the Buddha was. Having prostrated with their heads at his feet, they sat to one side.
It is the constant custom of all Buddhas to inquire of an incoming bhikṣu with these words:
"Was the summer retreat endured?
Was it sufficient?"
"Are you dwelling in peace and happiness?
Is alms-seeking not difficult for you, and are you not weary from the roads?
Now the Buddha likewise inquires after the bhikṣus in this way:
“Was the summer retreat endured?
Was it sufficient?
Did you dwell in peace and happiness?”
"Is it not difficult to beg for alms? Are you not weary from the road?
The bhikṣus replied, "We are content, dwelling in peace and happiness; begging for alms is not difficult, nor are we weary from the road."
The bhikṣus reported this matter in detail to the Buddha.
On account of these causes and conditions, the Buddha assembled the Saṃgha. Having assembled the Saṃgha, the Buddha rebuked the bhikṣus in various ways:
"You foolish people!..."
Like dwelling together with an enemy,
how can you say you live in peace and happiness?
Why are you called a bhikṣu?
"My assembly teaches according to the characteristics of the Dharma, yet you have accepted the 'dumb-dharma' (the practice of remaining silent).
After the Buddha had rebuked them with various causes and conditions, he said to the bhikṣus:
"From now on, you should not accept the dumb-dharma; if you do accept it, you shall incur a sthūlātyaya offense."
Why is this? Because not engaging in conversation is the practice of non-Buddhists.

From now on, it is permitted that at the conclusion of the summer retreat (*varṣā*), all bhikṣus shall assemble in one place and request another to perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation for criticism) by means of three matters.
What are the three?
Faults seen, faults heard, or faults suspected.
In this manner, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*.
With a single mind, assemble the Saṃgha. Once the Saṃgha has been assembled, one capable of acting as the *pravāraṇā*-officer should be appointed, and it should be announced in this way:
"Who is able to act as the *pravāraṇā*-officer for the Saṃgha?"
"If, among them, there should be one who says,
'I can,' the Buddha said:"
"If a bhikṣu possesses five unwholesome qualities, he should not perform the *pravāraṇā*. What are these five? First, performing the *pravāraṇā* out of attachment;

second, performing the *pravāraṇā* out of aversion; third, performing the *pravāraṇā* out of fear; fourth, performing the *pravāraṇā* out of delusion; fifth, not knowing whether the *pravāraṇā* has been performed or not."
A bhikkhu who is accomplished in five wholesome qualities should be appointed as a person to perform the *pravāraṇā*. What are the five? He does not perform the *pravāraṇā* out of attachment;

he does not perform the *pravāraṇā* out of aversion; he does not perform the *pravāraṇā* out of fear; he does not perform the *pravāraṇā* out of delusion; and he knows both when it is time for the *pravāraṇā* and when it is not.
At that time, one bhikṣu should announce among the Saṃgha:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

These bhikṣus, so-and-so and so-and-so, are capable of acting as the *pravāraṇā*-officers for the Saṃgha. If the time has come for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent; let the Saṃgha appoint these bhikṣus, so-and-so and so-and-so, as the *pravāraṇā*-officers for the Saṃgha."
Thus it is announced:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
These bhikṣus, so-and-so and so-and-so, are capable of acting as the *pravāraṇā* officers for the Saṃgha."
"Venerable [Name], this monk [Name] shall act as the one who performs the *pravāraṇā* for the Saṃgha.
Those elders who consent to [Name] and [Name] acting as the one who performs the *pravāraṇā* for the Saṃgha should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak."
“[Name], [Name] bhikṣu has completed his service as the one who facilitates the *pravāraṇā* for the Saṃgha. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.”
The *pravāraṇā* karmavācanā should be performed as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*. If the time has come for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, may the Saṃgha with one mind receive the *pravāraṇā*."
Thus he announces. At that time,
all the bhikṣus rise from their seats, kneel on the ground with their right knees,
and if the one performing the *pravāraṇā* is the senior monk (*sthavira*), he should rise from his seat, expose one shoulder, adjust his robe, and bow his body as he addresses the second senior monk:
"Elder! Today is the day for the invitation to admonish (*pravāraṇā*).

At that time, the second senior elder shall rise from his seat, adjust his robe to bare one shoulder, kneel with his right knee on the ground, and with both hands grasp the feet of the senior elder, speaking as follows:
"Venerable sir, please remember!

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s invitation for self-examination. I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the Venerable Saṃgha to speak to me regarding my invitation for self-examination. Out of compassion, please inform me if you have seen, heard, or suspect any offense in me."
"If I see my own fault, I shall remove it according to the Dharma.
Second: "Venerable one, please bear this in mind!"

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s Pravāraṇā; I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the Elder Saṃgha for their Pravāraṇā address. Out of compassion, please inform me if you have seen, heard, or suspect any offense committed by me.
"If I see my own fault, I shall eliminate it according to the Dharma.
Third: "Venerable one, please bear this in mind!"

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*. I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the venerable Saṃgha to grant me their *pravāraṇā* address. Out of compassion, please speak to me regarding any offense you have seen, heard, or suspect.
"If I see my own transgression, I shall eliminate it according to the Dharma.

If one of the junior monks is to perform the *pravāraṇā*, he should rise from his seat, bare his right shoulder, arrange his robe over one shoulder, kneel with his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and address the senior monk as follows:
"Today is the day for the *pravāraṇā*."
The Elder should likewise rise from his seat, drape his robe over one shoulder, kneel with his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and speak as follows:
"Venerable sir, please take note!

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s invitation for self-examination (*pravāraṇā*). I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the Venerable Saṃgha to speak to me regarding my conduct. Out of compassion, please inform me if you have seen, heard, or suspect any offense in me."
"If I see my fault, I shall eliminate it according to the Dharma.
Second: "Venerable one, bear this in mind!"

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s invitation for self-examination; I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the venerable Saṃgha to speak to me during the invitation for self-examination. Out of compassion, please inform me of any offense you have seen, heard, or suspect, so that I may address it.
"If I see my own fault, I shall eliminate it according to the Dharma.
Third: "Venerable one, please bear this in mind!"

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*. I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the venerable Saṃgha for *pravāraṇā*: may you speak to me regarding any offense you have seen, heard, or suspect, out of compassion.
"If I see my own transgression, I shall eliminate it according to the Dharma.
In this manner, the entire Saṃgha performs the *pravāraṇā* in succession.
When the entire Saṃgha has finished the *pravāraṇā*, those who act as the *pravāraṇā*-officers for the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā* together.
"When the *pravāraṇā* is concluded, one should go before the senior monk (*sthavira*) and announce:
'The Saṃgha has unanimously completed the *pravāraṇā*.
Thus spoke the Buddha to the bhikṣus.
"There are four kinds of *pravāraṇā*. What are the four?
First, the illegal separate *pravāraṇā*; second, the illegal united *pravāraṇā*; third, the legal separate *pravāraṇā*; and fourth, the legal united *pravāraṇā*."
Among these, the Buddha did not permit an unrighteous separate *pravāraṇā*.
The Buddha did not permit an unrighteous united *pravāraṇā*.
The Buddha did not permit a lawful separate *pravāraṇā*.
In this regard, there is a method for performing the *pravāraṇā* in combination, which the Buddha has permitted:

"If there is a residence where five bhikṣus are staying at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, those bhikṣus should assemble in one place, appoint one among them as the *pravāraṇā*-officer for the Saṃgha, and perform the *pravāraṇā* in detail."

“There is a residence where four bhikṣus are staying at the time of the *pravāraṇā*. These bhikṣus should not appoint anyone from among themselves to act as the *pravāraṇā*-officer for the Saṃgha; rather, these bhikṣus should assemble in one place and perform the *pravāraṇā* by means of the threefold formula. They should perform the *pravāraṇā* in this manner.”
The Elder should rise from his seat, adjust his robe to bare one shoulder, kneel with his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and speak thus:
"Venerable sir, please take note!

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*. I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the Venerable One’s *pravāraṇā* address. Out of compassion, please tell me of any offense you have seen, heard, or suspect regarding me."
"If I see my own fault, I shall eliminate it according to the Dharma. Second:
"Venerable one, remember!"

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*. I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the elders of the Saṃgha to speak to me regarding my *pravāraṇā*. Out of compassion, please inform me of any offense you have seen, heard, or suspect;
if I see such an offense, I shall remove it according to the Dharma.
Third: "Venerable sir, please remember!

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s invitation for self-examination (*pravāraṇā*). I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the venerable one to speak to me regarding my self-examination. Out of compassion, please tell me of any offense you have seen, heard, or suspect."
"If I see my own fault, I shall eliminate it according to the Dharma.
If he is of lower rank, he should rise from his seat, bare one shoulder, adjust his robes, kneel with both knees on the ground, and grasp the feet of the elder with both hands, speaking thus:
"Venerable sir, please take note!"

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*. I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the elders of the Saṃgha to speak to me regarding my *pravāraṇā*. Out of compassion, please speak to me if you see, hear, or suspect any offense in me.
If I see an offense, I shall remove it according to the Dharma.
The second [formula]:
"Venerable one, remember!

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s invitation for self-examination (*pravāraṇā*). I, the bhikṣu [name], invite the Venerable one to speak to me. If you see, hear, or suspect any offense in me, please speak to me out of compassion."
"If I see my fault, I shall remove it according to the Dharma. Third:
"Venerable one, remember!

Today is the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*. I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the elders of the Saṃgha to speak to me regarding my *pravāraṇā*. Out of compassion, please inform me if you see, hear, or suspect any offense in me.
If I see an offense, I shall remove it according to the Dharma.
"In this manner, these bhikṣus attain the *pravāraṇā*.
It is the same for three bhikṣus or two bhikṣus.

If there is only one bhikṣu in a residence, at the time of *pravāraṇā*, he should sweep the stūpa site and the place for the *pravāraṇā*, arrange the seats in order, prepare the fire, the lamps, the lamp-stands, the wicks, and the lamp-oil, and prepare the voting sticks (*śalākā*), reflecting thus:"
"If there are bhikṣus who have arrived but have not yet performed the *pravāraṇā*, those bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* together with them.
If one does not see them coming, one should stand on a high place within that area and look out.
If one sees a bhikṣu, one should call out to him:
"Come quickly, Venerable!
Today is the Saṃgha’s invitation ceremony (pravāraṇā)."
If he does not see [the monks], he should wait until evening, return to his original seat, and thus think and say aloud:
"Today the Saṃgha holds the Pravāraṇā; I too shall hold the Pravāraṇā today."
"In this way, a bhikṣu may perform the *pravāraṇā*.
While the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"This night has passed much; the time for the *pravāraṇā* has arrived."
A certain bhikṣu rose from his seat, bared one shoulder, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
the bhikṣus are ill and have not come.”
The Buddha said:
"One should accept the invitation to the *pravāraṇā*.
It should be accepted in this manner; one should speak to the sick bhikṣu as follows:"
"Grant the *pravāraṇā*.
He replied, "I grant it."
This is called obtaining *pravāraṇā*.
If one says:
"Proclaim the *pravāraṇā* for me within the Saṃgha."
This is called obtaining the *pravāraṇā*.
If it is given by moving the body, this is called obtaining the *pravāraṇā*.
If it is given by speaking with the mouth, this is called obtaining the *pravāraṇā*.
If he does not grant it by body nor by speech, he may not perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation for criticism) on his own authority.

At that time, the entire Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā* either at the side of the sick bhikṣu or bring him into the midst of the Saṃgha to perform the *pravāraṇā*; the bhikṣus should not perform the *pravāraṇā* separately.
If monks perform the *pravāraṇā* separately, all those monks incur an offense.

When there are two monks at a single residence performing the *pravāraṇā*, these two monks should not perform the *pravāraṇā* individually; rather, these two monks should perform the *pravāraṇā* by means of the threefold verbal formula together in one place.
The same applies to three or four monks.
"In a certain residence where there are five bhikṣus, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, these bhikṣus should not perform the *pravāraṇā* for themselves, nor should they grant the *pravāraṇā* to others.
These bhikṣus should assemble in one place and appoint a person to perform the *pravāraṇā* on behalf of the Saṃgha; they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in detail."

If there are more than five bhikṣus gathered in one place at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu who is old or infirm may, according to his own wish, take the *pravāraṇā* from another and give his own *pravāraṇā*.
If one person takes [the *pravāraṇā*] from another, this is called "obtaining the *pravāraṇā*."
If one person receives [the invitation] from two, three, or four people, this is called obtaining *pravāraṇā*.
According to however many people can remember and recognize the names [of those present], this is called obtaining *pravāraṇā*.
If the person from whom one seeks *pravāraṇā* (invitation to point out faults) does not wish to grant it, one should seek *pravāraṇā* from another.
If the person from whom one seeks *pravāraṇā* says: "I am a layperson; I am a *śrāmaṇera*;

I am not a *bhikṣu*; I am a follower of another path; I have been suspended for not seeing [an offense]; I have been suspended for not making amends; I have not removed evil views; I have been suspended and am not living in communion; I am subject to various forms of non-communion; I have committed a pārājika offense; I was originally a layperson; I am a eunuch; I have defiled a *bhikṣuṇī*; I am a desertionist; I have killed my father or mother; I have killed an *arhat*; I have caused a schism in the Saṃgha; I have shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind."
"One should further grant *pravāraṇā* to others.
If one accepts the *pravāraṇā* from another but does not depart once it is concluded, this is called 'not having arrived for *pravāraṇā*.
If one says:"

"I am a layperson; I am a śrāmaṇera; I am not a bhikṣu; I am of another path; I have not been seen [as guilty]; I have not been subjected to formal suspension (pravāsanīya); my evil and false views have not been removed; I have been suspended and am not living in communion; I am one who does not live in communion for various reasons; I have committed an offense involving defeat (pārājika); I was originally a layperson or a eunuch; I have defiled a bhikṣuṇī; I am a pārājika who has crossed over; I have killed my father or mother; I have killed an arhat; I have caused a schism in the Saṃgha; or I have, with an evil mind, shed the blood of a Buddha."
This is called "not arriving for the *pravāraṇā*.
If one has accepted another's invitation for the *pravāraṇā*, but fails to go because one or more of the eight difficulties arise, this is called "not arriving for the *pravāraṇā*."

Furthermore, having accepted another's invitation to the *pravāraṇā*, one does not depart because of negligence, laziness, sleep, or entering meditative absorption; this is called "not arriving for the *pravāraṇā*."
There are three causes and conditions by which one who has been invited to partake at will incurs an offense:
if they intentionally do not go, if they are lazy, or if they are negligent.
There are two causes and conditions by which there is no offense:
Whether one is asleep or has entered meditative absorption;
furthermore, having received another's invitation to the *pravāraṇā*, one arrives among the Saṃgha but does not announce the *pravāraṇā*—this is called "arrival at the *pravāraṇā*.
Or, having received another's invitation to the *pravāraṇā*, one arrives among the Saṃgha and says:

"I am a layperson; I am a śrāmaṇera; I am not a bhikṣu; I am a follower of another path; I have not been seen [to commit an offense]; I have not been formally expelled; my evil and false views have not been removed; I have been suspended and am not living in communion; I am one who lives in various forms of non-communion; I have committed a pārājika offense; I was originally a layperson or a paṇḍaka; I have defiled a bhikṣuṇī; I am a runaway from the army; I have killed my father or mother; I have killed an arhat; I have caused a schism in the Saṃgha; or I have shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind."
This is called "arriving at the *pravāraṇā*.

Furthermore, having received the *pravāraṇā* from another, one arrives in the midst of the Saṃgha; because one of the eight difficulties (*aṣṭau āpaddharmāḥ*) has arisen, one does not speak [the formal invitation]. This is called "arriving at the *pravāraṇā*."

Furthermore, having accepted another's invitation to the *pravāraṇā*, one goes before the Saṃgha but does not speak because of negligence, indolence, sleep, or entering into meditative concentration; this is called "arriving at the *pravāraṇā*."
In this regard, there are three causes and conditions by which one incurs an offense when taking part in another's *pravāraṇā*:
if one intentionally does not speak, if one is negligent, or if one is lazy. There are two causes and conditions by which there is no offense: [the other person] speaks first, or [one is] ill.
Whether he is asleep or in meditative absorption:

"There is a certain residence where, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, if a bhikṣu is seized by a king, or by a thief, or by an enemy, or by an enemy's faction, or by the faction of an enemy's faction, the Saṃgha should send a messenger to say to him:
'Today is the *pravāraṇā* of the Saṃgha; if this bhikṣu can come, or if he comes with his *pravāraṇā*, or if he goes beyond the boundary, we should not perform the *pravāraṇā* separately.'"
If that bhikṣu returns, or if he grants his own invitation to the Pavarana, or if he goes beyond the boundary, it is well.
If he does not do so, the bhikṣus should not perform the Pavarana separately.
If they perform the *pravāraṇā* separately, all the bhikṣus incur an offense.

Suppose there is a residence where, at the time of *pravāraṇā*, the entire community of bhikṣus has committed an offense but does not recognize it as such; except for one visiting bhikṣu who is pure and shares the same views with them.
If this visiting bhikṣu recognizes among the resident bhikṣus those who are virtuous and of good character, he should ask them:
"Venerable sirs!
If a bhikṣu commits such and such an act, what offense will he incur?"
He replied:
"If a bhikṣu performs such and such an act, he shall incur such and such an offense. He said:
"Elder! Do you yourself recall having done such a thing?
He replied:
"I recall that it is not only I alone who has incurred this offense; the entire Saṃgha has also incurred this offense.
The visiting bhikṣu said:
"Venerable One!..."
"What benefit do you derive from saying 'the entire Saṃgha'?
Why do you not repent of this offense according to the Dharma?
Having received these words from the visiting bhikṣu, the resident bhikṣu repented of that offense according to the Dharma.
When the other bhikṣus see this bhikṣu repenting, they too should likewise repent according to the Dharma.

If they act in this way, it is good; if they do not act thus, they should recognize whether an accusation would be beneficial or not, and if it would be unbeneficial, they must not persist in accusing him.

"If there is a residence where, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu remembers an offense he wishes to disclose, that bhikṣu should confess that offense according to the Dharma in the presence of another bhikṣu."
Having completed these tasks, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu has a doubt regarding a single offense. That bhikṣu should say to another bhikṣu:
'Venerable sir!'"
"I have a doubt regarding a transgression; I shall inquire about this matter later.
Having completed these formalities, one should perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to admonish); one should not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
If, at the time of the *pravāraṇā* in a certain residence, a monk remembers a transgression and wishes to confess it, that bhikṣu should quickly and with single-minded attention reflect:
"I shall later confess this offense according to the Dharma.
Having performed this, one should then proceed with the *pravāraṇā*; one should not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
If, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu has doubt regarding a single offense, that bhikṣu should quickly and with a focused mind reflect:
"Later, this offense shall be investigated.
Having acted thus, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, the entire community of bhikṣus has committed an offense. They are aware of this offense but are unable to obtain the purity of visiting bhikṣus to dwell together with them in shared view, nor can they perform a formal confession for this offense according to the Dharma."
These bhikṣus should dispatch one senior bhikṣu to the neighboring residence to arrive there quickly; having finished confessing this offense according to the Dharma, he should return and say:
"We have confessed this offense to you according to the Dharma."
"If these bhikṣus are able to accomplish this matter, it is well.
If they cannot accomplish it, a single bhikṣu within this Saṃgha should proclaim:
'Venerable Saṃgha, listen!'"

"We, the entire Saṃgha residing here, have committed an offense. Having recognized this offense, we were unable to attain purification; nor could we dwell together with visiting bhikṣus who share the same view regarding this offense and perform the confession according to the Dharma. Furthermore, we were unable to arrange for one of our resident bhikṣus to go quickly to a nearby monastery, confess this offense according to the Dharma there, and return. We shall now confess this offense according to the Dharma right here."
"If the time has come for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: if the Saṃgha later performs the repentance for this offense according to the Dharma, I shall thus announce it.
Having completed this, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, the entire Saṃgha has a doubt regarding a single offense. In this case, one bhikṣu should announce thus within the Saṃgha:
'Venerable Saṃgha, listen!'"
Regarding this matter, the entire Saṃgha residing here has a doubt concerning a single offense.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent and listen: the Saṃgha shall subsequently inquire into this matter.
Thus is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
"Having performed this rite, one should then perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation for criticism); one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.

Suppose at a certain residence, when the time for *pravāraṇā* has come, five or more resident monks have assembled at that place and are performing the *pravāraṇā*, and then monks from another residence arrive who are pure, dwell together, and share the same views in great numbers; these monks should perform the *pravāraṇā* again. Having done so, the original monks are without fault."

If, after the *pravāraṇā* has been completed by the bhikṣus, while no one has yet risen from their seats or departed, other bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, live together with them, and share the same views in great numbers, those bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; having done so, the former bhikṣus are without fault.

If, after the *pravāraṇā* has been completed by the bhikṣus, some have already departed while others have not yet departed, and further bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, dwell together with them, and share the same views in great number, those bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; having done so, the bhikṣus who were there first incur no offense.

If, after the *pravāraṇā* has been concluded by these bhikṣus, while all those seated have risen but not yet departed, other bhikṣus from a different residence arrive who are pure, dwell together with them, and share the same views in great numbers, then these bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; having done so, the former bhikṣus are without fault.
The same applies to those of equal status.

At a certain residence, when it is time for the *pravāraṇā* ceremony, five or more resident bhikṣus have assembled at that place to perform the *pravāraṇā*. If bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, living together, and hold the same views, though they are few in number, those bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.

If, after the *pravāraṇā* has been completed by the bhikṣus, while no one has yet risen from their seats or departed, bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, with whom they dwell together, and who hold the same views, though in small numbers, those [resident] bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* toward them using the threefold formula.

If, after the *pravāraṇā* has been concluded, some monks have already departed while others have not yet departed, and monks from another residence arrive who are pure, live together with them, and hold the same views—but are few in number—those who have not yet departed should perform the *pravāraṇā* by means of a threefold verbal formula in the presence of those monks.

If, after the *pravāraṇā* has been concluded by these bhikṣus, while they have all risen but not yet departed, other bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, with whom they dwell together, and who share the same views—even if they are few—if these bhikṣus can achieve harmony, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* extensively.
If harmony cannot be reached, one should go outside the boundary and perform the *pravāraṇā* by means of the three-fold proclamation.
If, while the resident bhikṣus are performing the *pravāraṇā*, other resident bhikṣus arrive—whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer—[the following applies].

If the number of visiting monks is equal to or greater than the resident monks, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if the number of visiting monks is fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.
This applies when visiting monks arrive while the resident monks are in the process of performing their *pravāraṇā*, whether the visitors are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If there are more [newly arrived monks], they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they are equal in number or fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.
If, while the resident monks are performing the *pravāraṇā*, other resident monks or guest monks arrive together—whether they are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer—[the following applies].
If there are many or an equal number [of resident monks], they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if there are fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.
If, while the guest monks are performing their *pravāraṇā*, more guest monks arrive—whether they be many, equal in number, or few—[the procedure shall be adjusted accordingly].
If the resident monks are more numerous, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they are equal in number or fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in due order.
This applies when resident monks arrive while visiting monks are in the midst of their *pravāraṇā*, whether the residents are more numerous, equal, or fewer.
If the number [of resident monks] is greater than or equal to [the visiting monks], they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.

When the visiting monks are performing their *pravāraṇā*, if the resident monks and the visiting monks arrive together—whether they are more numerous, equal in number, or fewer—the same procedure applies.
If they are equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they are fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.
If, while resident monks and visiting monks are performing the *pravāraṇā* together, more resident monks arrive—whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If they are equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they are fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.
If, while resident monks and visiting monks are performing the *pravāraṇā* together, more visiting monks arrive—whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If there are more [newly arrived bhikṣus], they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they are equal in number or fewer, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in sequence.
If, while resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus are performing the *pravāraṇā* together, more resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus arrive—whether they be more numerous, equal in number, or fewer.
If there are many or an equal number [of monks], they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if there are few, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* in succession.
"At a certain residence during the time of *pravāraṇā*, if there are five or more resident monks, they assemble at the place of *pravāraṇā* intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*."
Furthermore, if monks from another residence come who are pure, with whom one may dwell together and who share the same views in great numbers, they should think:
"The resident monks here, whether five or more, have assembled at the place for the *pravāraṇā* ceremony intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*; we too should perform the *pravāraṇā*."

If one performs the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to admonish) with the perception that [the assembly] is pure, the perception that it is according to the *vinaya*, or the perception that those who are separate from the group are actually part of the same group, and subsequently other resident bhikṣus arrive who are numerous, pure, co-resident, and of the same view, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; the former bhikṣus incur an offense.

If that bhikṣu has completed the *pravāraṇā* while perceiving [the assembly] as pure, perceiving it as being in accordance with the *vinaya*, or perceiving the separate group as being the same group, yet all those seated have not risen or departed; or if some have risen and departed while others have not; or if all have risen but not yet departed, and another bhikṣu comes from a different residence who is pure, dwells together with them, and shares the same views in great number, then that bhikṣu should perform the *pravāraṇā* again, and the former bhikṣu incurs an offense.
“At a certain residence, when it is time for the *pravāraṇā*, five or more resident bhikṣus have assembled at the place of the *pravāraṇā* intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*.
Then, bhikṣus from another residence arrive, who are pure, dwell together, and share the same views, and they are numerous. They think:
‘Five or more resident bhikṣus have assembled at this place of *pravāraṇā* intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*; we should not perform the *pravāraṇā* here.’”
That bhikṣu says, "I perform the *pravāraṇā*.
With an impure mind, he regrets [the act] while perceiving the separate assembly as the same assembly; herein he performs the *pravāraṇā*.

If other bhikṣus from a different residence arrive who are pure, with whom one may dwell together and who share the same views in great numbers, those bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; the former bhikṣus incur an offense.

If those bhikṣus, with impure minds, perform the *pravāraṇā* while perceiving themselves as a separate group though they are part of the same assembly, and while all those seated have not yet risen or departed; or some have risen and departed while others have not; or some have risen but not yet departed; and then other bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, living together, and share the same views, being more numerous than the former—those bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again, and the former bhikṣus incur an offense.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, five or more resident bhikṣus have gathered at the place of the *pravāraṇā* intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*. Then, bhikṣus from another residence arrive who are pure, live together with them, and share the same views, and they are numerous. Those bhikṣus think:
'Whether we are appropriate or inappropriate [to do so], should we perform the *pravāraṇā* here?'"

If one suspects whether they are pure or impure, yet perceives them as being of a different group or the same group, and subsequently other monks from a different residence arrive who are pure, live together, and share the same views in great numbers, those original monks should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; the former monks incur an offense.

If, while doubting whether [the assembly] is pure or impure, one performs the *pravāraṇā* with the perception that it is a separate group or the same group, and the assembly has finished the *pravāraṇā*, yet some members of the assembly have not risen or departed from their seats, some have risen and departed while others have not, and some have all risen but not yet departed—should another monk from a different residence arrive who is pure, shares the same dwelling, and holds the same views, and this new group is numerous—then these monks must perform the *pravāraṇā* again; the former monks incur an offense.

"At a certain residence, during the time of the *pravāraṇā*, five or more resident monks have gathered at the place of the *pravāraṇā* intending to perform the ceremony. Then, monks from another residence arrive who are numerous, pure, living together, and of like views. Having heard this, they think:

'Monks from another residence have arrived who are numerous, pure, living together, and of like views; this will lead to the dissolution, abandonment, and separation [of our group]. I have no need for these monks.'"

If, with the intent to cause a schism in the Saṃgha, one performs the *pravāraṇā* while perceiving a separate group as being the same group, and other resident bhikṣus arrive who are pure, dwell together, and share the same views in great numbers, those bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again. The former bhikṣu incurs a *sthūlātyaya* offense because he has nearly caused a schism in the Saṃgha.

If these bhikṣus, desiring to cause a schism in the Saṃgha, perform the *pravāraṇā* while harboring the perception that they are a separate group rather than a unified assembly—and if, while all those seated have not yet risen or departed, some have risen and departed while others have not, or some have risen while others have not departed, another group of bhikṣus arrives from a different residence who are pure, live together in harmony, and share the same views in great numbers—then these bhikṣus must perform the *pravāraṇā* again. The former bhikṣus incur a *sthūlātyaya* offense because they were close to causing a schism in the Saṃgha.
If, while the resident bhikṣus are performing the *pravāraṇā*, other resident bhikṣus arrive who are either more numerous or equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again.
If, while the resident bhikṣus are performing the *pravāraṇā*, guest bhikṣus arrive who are either more numerous or equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again.

If, at the time of the *pravāraṇā* of the resident monks, both resident and guest monks arrive together, and if they are equal in number or the guests are more numerous, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed again.
If, at the time of the *pravāraṇā* of the guest monks, guest monks arrive, and if they are equal in number or more numerous, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed again.
When visiting bhikṣus are performing the *pravāraṇā*, if resident bhikṣus arrive who are numerous or equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again.
When visiting bhikṣus are performing the *pravāraṇā*, if both resident and visiting bhikṣus arrive together who are numerous or equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again.
When resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus perform the *pravāraṇā* together, if resident bhikṣus arrive who are either more numerous or equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again.
When resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus perform the *pravāraṇā* together, if visiting bhikṣus arrive who are either more numerous or equal in number, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again.

When resident bhikṣus and visiting bhikṣus perform the *pravāraṇā* together, if both the resident and visiting bhikṣus arrive together and their numbers are either equal or the visitors are more numerous, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* again.

"If the resident bhikṣus have exceeded fourteen days and the visiting bhikṣus have fallen short of fifteen days, the visiting bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus; on this day, they should perform the *pravāraṇā*."

If the resident bhikṣus are fourteen days short and the visiting bhikṣus are fifteen days ahead, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus; on this day, they should not perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If the resident bhikṣus are numerous on the fifteenth day while the visiting bhikṣus are few on the first day, the visiting bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus and perform the *pravāraṇā* on that very day.

If the resident bhikṣus are few on the fifteenth day while the visiting bhikṣus are many on the first day, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus out of the boundary to perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If the visiting bhikṣus are many on the fourteenth day while the resident bhikṣus are few on the fifteenth day, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus; they should perform the *pravāraṇā* on that very day.

If the visiting bhikṣus have one day less than fourteen days remaining and the resident bhikṣus have one day more than fifteen days remaining, the visiting bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus; on this day, they should not perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If the visiting bhikṣus are numerous on the fifteenth day while the resident bhikṣus are few on the first day, the resident bhikṣus should follow the visiting bhikṣus and perform the *pravāraṇā* on that very day.

If the number of visiting *bhikṣus* on the fifteenth day is fewer than the number of resident *bhikṣus* on the first day, the visiting *bhikṣus* should follow the resident *bhikṣus* in leaving the boundary to perform the *pravāraṇā*.

In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, the resident *bhikṣus* hear the voices of the visiting *bhikṣus* or signs of their presence—whether the sound of footsteps, the sound of staffs, the sound of leather sandals, or the voices of strangers—and yet these resident *bhikṣus* do not seek them out or look for them before performing the *pravāraṇā*, the resident *bhikṣus* incur an offense.
If one seeks [to perform] a *pravāraṇā* that is not invited, the resident bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If one seeks it but cannot obtain it and there is doubt regarding the *pravāraṇā*, the resident bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If one seeks it but cannot obtain it and there is no doubt regarding the *pravāraṇā*, the resident bhikṣu is without offense.
If one succeeds in finding these visiting bhikṣus, one should perform the *pravāraṇā* with a single-minded joy; in this way, the resident bhikṣus are without fault.

If, at a certain residence during the time of *pravāraṇā*, the visiting bhikṣus hear the voices of the resident bhikṣus—whether it be the sound of keys, the sound of an adze, the sound of an axe, or the sound of reciting the scriptures—and yet these visiting bhikṣus do not seek them out or look for them to perform the *pravāraṇā*, the visiting bhikṣus incur a fault.
If he seeks it and does not obtain the invitation to retire at will (*pravāraṇā*), the visiting bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If he seeks it and cannot obtain it, yet suspects that the invitation to retire at will will be granted, the visiting bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If he seeks it and cannot obtain it, and has no suspicion that the invitation to retire at will will be granted, the visiting bhikṣu is without offense.
If one succeeds in finding these resident bhikṣus, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* with a single-minded joy; in this way, the visiting bhikṣus will be without fault.

In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, the resident bhikṣus see the signs of visiting bhikṣus and the reasons for their arrival, yet they do not recognize their robes and bowls, nor their staffs, nor their leather oil-bags, sandals, or needle-cases. If these resident bhikṣus do not seek them out or search for them before performing the *pravāraṇā*, those resident bhikṣus incur an offense.
If he seeks [the invitation] but it is not granted as a *pravāraṇā* (invitation to criticize), the resident bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If he seeks it but cannot obtain it and there is doubt regarding the *pravāraṇā*, the resident bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If he seeks it but cannot obtain it and there is no doubt regarding the *pravāraṇā*, the resident bhikṣu is without offense.
If one succeeds in finding these visiting bhikṣus, one should perform the *pravāraṇā* with single-minded joy; in this way, the resident bhikṣus will be free from fault.

In a certain residence during the time of *pravāraṇā*, the visiting bhikṣus perceive the signs of resident bhikṣus—the causes for the arrival of resident bhikṣus—such as the ground having been freshly swept and watered, or beds and seats being arranged in order. If these visiting bhikṣus do not seek out or look for [the residents] to perform the *pravāraṇā*, the visiting bhikṣus incur a fault.
If one seeks [to perform the *pravāraṇā*] but it is not called "self-indulgence" (*svacchanda*), the visiting bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If one seeks [to perform the *pravāraṇā*] but fails to obtain it and yet acts as if it were "self-indulgence," the visiting bhikṣu incurs an offense.
If one seeks [the regular monks] but cannot find them, one may perform the *pravāraṇā* without hesitation; the visiting bhikṣus are without fault.
If one finds these resident bhikṣus, they should perform the *pravāraṇā* together with a single mind and in joy; in this way, the visiting bhikṣus are without fault.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, if a bhikṣu—whether he has been accused by another or not, whether he has been made to remember [his offense] or not—declares of himself:
'I have committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense.'"
That bhikṣu should be granted the parivāsa (probation), but it is not accomplished [if done otherwise].
In this matter, one bhikṣu should announce within the saṃgha:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."

In this case, there is a monk residing in a particular place who—whether another person has accused him or not, whether he has been made to remember or not—confesses himself to have committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense. This monk should be granted the period of *parivāsa*; if it is not granted, it is not validly granted.
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, the Saṃgha shall grant this bhikṣu *parivāsa* (probation).
Thus is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Having performed this, they should then proceed with the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu—whether he has been accused by another or not, whether he has been made to remember [the offense] or not—declares of himself that he possesses a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense."
If this bhikṣu should be granted *mānatva*, or should be granted *mūlāpakarṣa*, or should be granted *āvarhaṇa*, yet it is not accomplished as such,
then within that assembly of bhikṣus, one bhikṣu should announce: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."

In this dwelling there is a bhikṣu who, whether he has been accused by another or not, whether he has been made to remember [the offense] or not, declares himself to have committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense.
This bhikṣu should be granted *mānāpya*, *paryuṣitaparivāsa*, and *āvarhaṇa*, yet it has not been successfully granted.

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the Saṃgha shall subsequently grant this bhikṣu *mānāpya*, shall grant him *paryuṣitaparivāsa*, and shall grant him *āvarhaṇa*.
Thus one should announce it.
Having performed this, one should then proceed with the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.

At a certain residence during the time of *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu—whether he has been accused by another or not, whether he has been made to remember [his offense] or not—declares himself to have committed a *tisa-karaṇīya* offense.
Regarding this matter, they disputed it; some bhikṣus said,
"In this case, one should undergo confession," while other bhikṣus said:
"One should give rise to remorse regarding this matter.
In this regard, one bhikṣu should announce within the Saṃgha:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."

In this dwelling place, there is a bhikṣu who, whether he has been accused by another or not, or whether he has been made to remember [the offense] or not, declares himself to have committed a *tisa-karaṇīya* offense.
Regarding this matter, they disputed it; some bhikṣus said,
"This matter should be confessed," while other bhikṣus said:
"One should give rise to remorse in one's mind regarding this matter.

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent and listen: if this bhikṣu obtains another bhikṣu who dwells in purity with him and shares the same views, he shall confess this offense before that bhikṣu in accordance with the Dharma.
Thus one should announce.
Having performed this, one should proceed with the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.

At a certain residence during the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu—whether he has been accused by another or not, whether he has been made to remember [his offense] or not—confesses himself to having committed a *tisa-karaṇīya* offense.
Regarding this matter, they disputed it; one bhikṣu said,
"This is a pāyattika offense," while another bhikṣu said:
"This is an offense of pāṭidesanīya.
In this regard, one bhikṣu should announce within the saṃgha:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
In this dwelling place there is a bhikṣu who, whether accused by another or not, whether reminded of it or not, confesses himself to have committed a *tisa-kāraṇī* offense.
Regarding this matter, they disputed it; some bhikṣus said,
"This is a pāyattika offense," while other bhikṣus said:
"This is an offense of *pāṭidesanīya*.
If the Saṃgha deems it the right time and grants its consent, let this bhikṣu confess this offense according to the Dharma before another bhikṣu who is pure and dwells with him in the same view."
Thus one should announce it.
Having done so, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.

At a certain residence during the time of *pravāraṇā*, whether a bhikṣu has been accused by another or not, whether he has been made to remember [his offense] or not, he himself declares that he has committed a *tisa-karaṇīya* offense.
Regarding this matter, they disputed it; some bhikṣus said,
"This offense is a *śeṣa* (residual) and can be remedied," while other bhikṣus said:
"One with no remainder cannot be cured.
In this context, it is said:
"One with a remainder can be cured; such a person should participate in the *pravāraṇā* together with the community."
In this context, it is said:
"One who has committed an offense that leaves no remainder and is incurable should not participate in the *pravāraṇā* ceremony together with others.
Such a person should set aside the *pravāraṇā* and depart; they should not engage in quarreling or mutual recrimination.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, there is a bhikṣu who speaks of another bhikṣu’s offense—whether based on what he has seen, heard, or suspected.

If the other bhikṣus know that this person who speaks of another’s offense is impure in his bodily actions, capable of sexual misconduct, capable of stealing, capable of taking human life, capable of falsely claiming superhuman states (*uttarimanussa-dhamma*), capable of emitting semen, capable of physical contact with the bodies of others, capable of killing living plants, capable of eating at improper times, or capable of drinking liquor, they should not trust the words of this bhikṣu when dealing with the punishment for another’s offense."
The Saṃgha should say to him:
"Venerable one, do not be angry; do not fight; do not dispute; do not speak ill of one another.
The Saṃgha should not count such shameless persons [among its members].
The Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one should not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
"At a certain residence during the time of *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu spoke of another bhikṣu’s offense—whether seen, heard, or suspected."

The bhikṣus knew that this elder was one who spoke of the faults of others, whose verbal karma was impure, and who was capable of lying: claiming to know what he did not know, claiming not to know what he did know; claiming to have seen what he had not seen, claiming not to have seen what he had seen; claiming not to doubt what he doubted, and claiming to doubt what he did not doubt.
The Saṃgha should say to that bhikṣu: "Venerable one! You should not believe such words of a bhikṣu and thereby punish another for their offense."
"Do not be angry, do not fight, do not dispute, and do not speak against one another.
Such shameless persons, the Saṃgha should not count;
the Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*, and should not create obstacles to their *pravāraṇā*.

"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu spoke of another bhikṣu’s offense—whether seen, heard, or suspected. The other bhikṣus knew that this elder who spoke of another’s offense was impure in his physical actions and impure in his verbal actions;

that he was capable of sexual misconduct, capable of stealing, capable of taking human life, capable of falsely claiming superhuman states (*uttarimanussa-dhamma*), capable of intentionally emitting semen, capable of intentionally touching a woman’s body, capable of killing living plants, capable of eating at improper times, and capable of drinking alcohol; and that he was also capable of lying: saying he knew what he did not know, saying he did not know what he knew, saying he saw what he did not see, saying he did not see what he saw, saying he had no doubt where he had doubts, and saying he had doubts where he had none."
The Saṃgha should say to that bhikṣu: "Venerable one! One should not believe such words of a bhikṣu when it comes to adjudicating the offenses of others."
"Do not be angry, do not fight, do not dispute, and do not speak against one another.
Monks, you should not count such shameless persons;
the Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*, and you should not create obstacles to their *pravāraṇā*.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a bhikṣu spoke of another bhikṣu’s offense—whether seen, heard, or suspected.
The other bhikṣus knew that this elder who spoke of the other’s offense was pure in his physical actions."

This elder is able to refrain from sexual misconduct, theft, taking human life, claiming superhuman attainments for himself, intentional emission of semen, intentional contact with the body of a woman, killing living plants, eating at improper times, and drinking alcohol; yet this elder possesses little wisdom, lacks decisiveness, and is not well-informed, such that he may also declare what is non-Dharma to be Dharma, what is Dharma to be non-Dharma, what is unwholesome to be wholesome, and what is wholesome to be unwholesome.
The Saṃgha should say to that bhikṣu: "Venerable one! One should not believe such words of a bhikṣu and thereby punish another for their offense."
"Do not be angry, do not fight, do not quarrel, and do not speak against one another.
Such people of little wisdom should not be counted by the Saṃgha.
The Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*; it should not create obstacles to the *pravāraṇā*.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a monk speaks of another monk’s offense—whether seen, heard, or suspected.

If the monks know that this elder’s verbal karma is pure, and that this elder cannot fail to know what he knows, nor say he knows what he does not know; cannot fail to see what he has seen, nor say he sees what he has not seen; cannot fail to doubt what he doubts, nor say he does not doubt what he doubts; and that this elder possesses little wisdom, is indecisive, and lacks skillful knowledge; and that this person can likewise speak of what is non-Dharma as Dharma, Dharma as non-Dharma, the wholesome as unwholesome, and the unwholesome as wholesome—then the words of such a monk should not be trusted when it comes to adjudicating the offenses of others."
The Saṃgha should say to that bhikṣu: "Venerable one!
Do not be angry; do not quarrel; do not dispute; do not speak against one another."
"In this way, one who possesses little wisdom should not be counted among the Saṃgha.
The Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*; it should not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
At a certain residence during the time of *pravāraṇā*, a single bhikṣu spoke of another bhikṣu’s offense to other bhikṣus—whether based on what he had seen, heard, or suspected."

The monks know that this elder who speaks of others' offenses is pure in his bodily actions and pure in his verbal actions. This elder is able to refrain from sexual misconduct, theft, and intentionally taking human life;

he does not falsely claim superhuman attainments; he does not intentionally emit semen; he does not intentionally touch a woman's body; he does not kill even a blade of grass; he does not eat at improper times; he does not drink alcohol; he does not claim to know what he does not know, or claim not to know what he knows; he does not claim to see what he has not seen, or claim not to see what he has seen; he does not say he doubts what he does not doubt, or say he does not doubt what he doubts. Yet this elder possesses little wisdom, lacks decisiveness, and is not well-informed; such a person is also capable of calling what is non-Dharma "Dharma," what is Dharma "non-Dharma," what is wholesome "unwholesome," and what is unwholesome "wholesome."
The Saṃgha should say this to that bhikṣu: "Venerable one! One should not believe such words of a bhikṣu when adjudicating the offenses of others."
"Do not be angry; do not fight; do not dispute; do not speak against one another.
Such a person of little wisdom should not be counted among the Saṃgha.
The Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*; it should not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
"In a certain residence, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, one bhikṣu spoke of another bhikṣu’s offense—whether seen, heard, or suspected."

The monks know that this elder who speaks of another’s offenses is pure in bodily action and pure in verbal action; that this elder is incapable of sexual misconduct, theft, intentionally taking human life, claiming superhuman attainments for himself, intentional emission of semen, intentional contact with a woman’s body, killing even a blade of grass, eating at improper times, drinking alcohol, or being ignorant while claiming to know, knowing while claiming not to know, not seeing while claiming to see, seeing while claiming not to see, doubting while claiming not to doubt, or not doubting while claiming to doubt. This elder speaks of another’s offenses; he is a wise man, a person of certainty, and one who knows well. Such a person would not declare what is not Dharma to be Dharma, nor what is Dharma to be non-Dharma; he would not declare what is wholesome to be unwholesome, nor what is unwholesome to be wholesome.
At that time, the elder should calmly and discreetly ask and discreetly instruct him:
"Elder, when you spoke of another's offense, did you see it with your own eyes, hear it with your own ears, or suspect it in your mind?"
If that elder says,
"I saw it with my eyes," the bhikṣus should ask him:
"If it is seen by the eye, one should not say that it is heard by the ear or doubted by the mind.
What is seen? Where is it seen? How is it seen?"
"What are you doing? For what reason have you come there?
If that person should say:
"I heard it.
"One should not say that one saw it with the eye but has doubts; rather, state what was heard and where it was heard."
What is hearing?
What does hearing do?
Is it heard from the male side?
Did you hear it from a woman?
Did you hear it from a man?
Or did you hear it from a person with both sexual organs?
If one says, "My mind has doubts," [the teacher] should say:
"One should not say that it was seen by the eye or heard by the ear; what is it that you doubt?"
Where is there doubt?
How is there doubt?
What is the object of doubt?

Is there doubt regarding bodily offenses, doubt regarding verbal offenses, or doubt regarding whether an offense is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* (requiring suspension) or not a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*, or doubt regarding whether it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* or not?
Is there doubt as to whether one is in a village or in the wilderness? Where is the doubt?
"In this manner, they shall discreetly inquire and discreetly instruct him. If that elder monk is found to have spoken the truth, the bhikṣus should with one mind discipline that offending bhikṣu.
If the offending bhikṣu says:
'I am a layman (avadātavasana),' [he should be dealt with accordingly]."
The Saṃgha should say:
"Go out! The Saṃgha should then perform the *pravāraṇā*;
they must not create an obstacle to the performance of the *pravāraṇā*.

"If one says: 'I am a śrāmaṇera, not a bhikṣu; I am of a different path; I have not been seen to be suspended; I have not been subjected to suspension; I hold evil and false views; my suspension has not been removed; I do not live in communion; I live in various forms of non-communion; I have committed a pārājika offense; I was originally a layperson; I am a eunuch; I have defiled a bhikṣuṇī; I am a pārājika who has crossed over; I have killed my father or mother; I have killed an arhat; I have caused a schism in the Saṃgha; I am one who has shed the blood of a Buddha with an evil mind.'"
The Sangha should say: "Go out!
The bhikṣus should then perform the *pravāraṇā*, and they must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*.
Once all preliminary matters have been completed, the Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*.
If the *sammukhavinaya* (settlement in the presence) is appropriate, it should be granted; once granted, [the procedure is complete].
If the *smṛtivinaya* (settlement by recollection) is appropriate, it should be granted; once granted, [the procedure is complete].
The *amūḍhavinaya* (verdict of sanity) should be granted; it has been granted.
The *pratijñānavinaya* (verdict of confession) should be granted; it has been granted.
The *tattvānusaraṇavinaya* (verdict of searching for the truth) should be granted; it has been granted.
If the *tassapāpiyasikā* (formal act of further censure) should be granted, it shall be granted;
once granted, if that bhikṣu should be subject to the *tarjanīya-karman* (act of reprimand), it shall be granted;
once granted, if he should be subject to the *nissaya-karman* (act of dependence), it shall be granted.
If the *pravāsanīya-karman* (act of banishment) is to be performed, it is performed; if the *tarjanīya-karman* (act of reprimand) is to be performed, it is performed;
if the *adarśanāyotkṣepaṇīya-karman* (act of suspension for not acknowledging an offense) is to be performed, it is performed;
if the *parivāsa-karman* (act of probation) is to be performed, it is performed.
If the *mānatva* karmavācanā should be granted, it is granted;
if the *yadbhūyaḥparyuṣita* karmavācanā should be granted, it is granted;
if the *āvarhaṇa* karmavācanā should be granted, it is granted.
The Saṃgha should perform the *pravāraṇā*.

"If a monk dwelling in retreat hears that there are monks at another residence who have become angry, quarreling, disputing, and speaking abusively, and who intend to come here to obstruct the *pravāraṇā* of the monks in this place..."

The monks should perform the *poṣadha* twice, thrice, or four times in quick succession; they should appoint someone to perform the *pravāraṇā* for the Saṃgha, and that person should perform the *pravāraṇā* in detail.

If those monks accomplish this by performing the *poṣadha* twice, thrice, or four times in quick succession, and appoint someone to perform the *pravāraṇā* for the Saṃgha so that the *pravāraṇā* is performed in detail, it is excellent.

If it is not accomplished, and if the monks hear that those monks have come from there because they were quarreling, disputing, and exchanging harsh words out of anger, for the purpose of obstructing the *pravāraṇā*,
then at that time they should assemble quickly and appoint persons to perform the *pravāraṇā* in detail.
If the monks are in haste, they should assemble quickly; if there is someone capable of performing the *pravāraṇā*, it is well that he perform the *pravāraṇā* in detail.

If this is not possible, and if the resident monks hear that those monks have come from a place of anger, strife, contention, and mutual abuse to enter their territory, then at that time the resident monks should welcome them with a single-minded, gentle voice, inquire after their welfare with joy, and for them carry the robes and bowls, open the rooms, and show them the bedding, saying:
"Venerable sirs!"
"These are your beds and seats: coarse rope-cots, fine rope-cots, and bedding. You should occupy them according to the seniority of the elders.
Furthermore, you should provide therein the requisites for bathing, firewood, soap-nuts, hot water, and ointments of ghee and oil."

When the visiting bhikṣus have finished entering the bathhouse, the resident bhikṣus should go outside the boundary and appoint someone to act as the one who performs the *pravāraṇā* for the Saṃgha through a broad *pravāraṇā*.
It would be well if the resident bhikṣus could accomplish this matter.
If it is not accomplished, the resident bhikṣus should say to the visiting bhikṣus:
"Venerable sirs!
We are performing the poṣadha but not the pravāraṇā; at the next poṣadha time, we shall perform the pravāraṇā."
The visiting bhikṣu said to the resident bhikṣu:
"Venerable sir!
At the time of the subsequent poṣadha, you should not perform the *prātimokṣa* recitation. If there is anything to be said, say it today; for what purpose would it be?"
"We have been permitted by the Buddha to perform the *pravāraṇā* [invitation for criticism], but this matter is not permissible.
The resident bhikṣus should say to the visiting bhikṣus:
"Set aside the resident bhikṣus; you yourselves must know the time for the *pravāraṇā*."
"If it is a visiting bhikṣu, it is best for him to depart for another place at that time.
If he does not depart, the resident bhikṣus should say to the visiting bhikṣu:

'We do not perform the *pravāraṇā* at the later *poṣadha*; we perform the *pravāraṇā* in the eighth month or the fourth month, as we receive abundant offerings during our final month of the summer retreat.'"
If a visiting bhikṣu says to a resident bhikṣu:
"Venerable sir!
You are not permitted to perform the *pravāraṇā* during the eight months or the four months; if there is any matter to be discussed, speak of it today—for what purpose?"
"We have been permitted by the Buddha to perform the *pravāraṇā* (self-examination), but this matter is not permissible.
The resident bhikṣus should say to the visiting bhikṣus:
"You should set aside the resident bhikṣus and know for yourselves the time for the *pravāraṇā*."
"If it is a visiting bhikṣu, it would be best for him to depart for another place at this time.
If he does not depart, he should leave without performing the *pravāraṇā* ceremony here; for we should not harbor anger, engage in strife, or speak with mutual contention."
"If there is a sick bhikṣu who obstructs a healthy bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*, the Saṃgha should say to that sick bhikṣu:
'Elder, you are ill; do not obstruct the healthy bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*.'"
"Why is this? Because the sick person has little peace and comfort.
If there is a healthy bhikṣu who obstructs a sick bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*, the Saṃgha should say to that healthy bhikṣu:
"Elder! Do not obstruct the *pravāraṇā* of the sick bhikṣu. Why is that?..."
"Because the sick person has little peace and comfort.
If a sick bhikṣu sends a messenger to stop a healthy bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*, the Saṃgha should say to that messenger:
"Venerable one!..."
Do not accept the words of a sick person to obstruct the *pravāraṇā* of a healthy bhikṣu. Why?
Because the sick person possesses little peace and stability.
The messenger went to the side of the sick monk and said:
"Venerable sir!
The Sangha has issued an injunction: you must not obstruct a healthy bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā* while you are ill."
"Why is this? Because the patient has little comfort.
If the patient speaks thus as a refusal, that sick bhikṣu incurs the offense of *duṣkṛta*.
If one acts as a messenger for a sick person to obstruct the *pravāraṇā* of a healthy bhikṣu, that messenger incurs the offense of *duṣkṛta*.
It is the same when a healthy bhikṣu sends a messenger to obstruct the *pravāraṇā* of a sick bhikṣu.
“There are four kinds of unlawful ways of obstructing the *pravāraṇā*, and four kinds of lawful ways of obstructing the *pravāraṇā*.
What are the four unlawful ways of obstructing the *pravāraṇā*?

First, obstructing the *pravāraṇā* on grounds of groundless charges of broken precepts; second, on grounds of groundless charges of broken right view; third, on grounds of groundless charges of broken right livelihood; and fourth, on grounds of groundless charges of broken decorum.”
These are the four unrighteous grounds for withholding the *pravāraṇā*. What are the four righteous grounds for withholding the *pravāraṇā*?

First, there is the ground of breaking the precepts with a basis for accusation; second, there is the ground of breaking right view with a basis for accusation; third, there is the ground of breaking right livelihood with a basis for accusation; and fourth, there is the ground of breaking proper conduct with a basis for accusation. These are the grounds for withholding the *pravāraṇā*.
"These are the four matters that obstruct the *pravāraṇā*.
While the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"From now on, I permit the *pravāraṇā* to be performed with one recitation or two recitations; previously, I had permitted the *pravāraṇā* to be performed with three recitations."
If, during the first recitation of the *pravāraṇā*, one objects before it has been completed, this is an illegal obstruction of the *pravāraṇā*.
If one objects after the first recitation is finished, this is a legal obstruction of the *pravāraṇā*.
If, when the two-fold invitation (pravāraṇā) is being recited, one objects before the first recitation has been completed, this is an illegal obstruction of the invitation.
If one objects after the first recitation has been completed, this is also an illegal obstruction of the invitation.
If one interrupts before the second proclamation is finished, it is an illegal interruption of the *pravāraṇā*.
If one interrupts after the second proclamation is finished, it is a legal interruption of the *pravāraṇā*.
If one interrupts during the third proclamation of the *pravāraṇā* before the first [of the three] proclamations is finished, it is an illegal interruption of the *pravāraṇā*.
If one objects when the first recitation has finished, it is an illegal obstruction of the *pravāraṇā*.
If one objects when the second recitation has not yet finished, it is an illegal obstruction of the *pravāraṇā*.
If one objects when the second recitation has finished, it is an illegal obstruction of the *pravāraṇā*.
If an interruption occurs before the three recitations are completed, it is an illegal interruption of the *pravāraṇā*.
If an interruption occurs after the three recitations are completed, it is a legal interruption of the *pravāraṇā*.
"Where did the Buddha permit that the *pravāraṇā* should be performed with only one recitation?"
For example, at a time of *pravāraṇā* (invitation for criticism) when there is a great assembly in a single residence, the monks within that Saṃgha think to themselves:

"This is a great assembly of the Saṃgha in this residence; if we perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting it three times, the night will pass too long and we shall not be able to complete the *pravāraṇā*."
"If the time has come for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the Saṃgha shall perform the *pravāraṇā* by a single proclamation.
This is the formal announcement (*jñapti*).

Having performed it thus, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one should not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*. In this manner, the residence should perform the *pravāraṇā* by a single proclamation.

“Suppose, at the time of the *pravāraṇā* ceremony in a certain residence, a king or one like a king sits among the bhikṣus desiring to hear the Dharma. In that situation, the bhikṣus spend much of the night expounding the Dharma. The bhikṣus reflect:
‘In this residence, a king or one like a king sits among the bhikṣus desiring to hear the Dharma, and here the bhikṣus have spent much of the night expounding the Dharma.’”
"If we were to perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting three times, the night would pass too late for us to complete it.
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha, being patient and attentive, grant permission for the Saṃgha to perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting once."

Having made this announcement, one should then perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create obstacles to the *pravāraṇā*. In such a residence, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed by a single recitation.

“Suppose at a certain residence, during the time of the *pravāraṇā*, a great amount of offerings is received. Among the monks there, the night becomes excessively long due to their engaging in various activities.

The monks reflect: ‘In this residence, the Saṃgha has received a great deal of offerings; however, because the monks engage in various activities, the night has become excessively long. If we perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting it three times, the night will be too long and we will not be able to complete the *pravāraṇā*.’”
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, the Saṃgha shall perform the *pravāraṇā* by a single proclamation.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Having performed this, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one should not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*. In such a residence, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed by a single proclamation.

"Suppose, at the time of the *pravāraṇā* ceremony in a certain residence, there are two Dharma-teachers who possess eloquence in meaning (*artha-pratibhāna*), eloquence in names (*nāma-pratibhāna*), eloquence in phrasing (*vyañjana-pratibhāna*), and eloquence in ready response (*pratibhāna*).
When these two bhikṣus preach the Dharma, much of the night passes by. The other bhikṣus reflect:

'In this residence there are these two Dharma-teachers with eloquence in meaning, names, phrasing, and ready response; because these bhikṣus spend so much of the night preaching the Dharma, if we were to perform the three proclamations for *pravāraṇā* here, much of the night would pass and we would be unable to complete the *pravāraṇā*.'"
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, the Saṃgha shall perform the *pravāraṇā* by a single recitation.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Having performed this, one should then perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*. In such a residence, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed by a single recitation.

"Just as when, during the *pravāraṇā* ceremony at a certain residence, various matters—whether all four or even just one—arise for the bhikṣus, because of this the night passes for much of its duration. The bhikṣus reflect:
'In this residence, various matters—whether all four or even just one—arise for the bhikṣus; because of this, the night passes for much of its duration.'"
"If we were to perform the *pravāraṇā* three times within this [period], the night would pass too quickly and we would not be able to perform the *pravāraṇā*.
Therefore, if the time has come for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, let the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā* with a single recitation."

Having made this announcement in this manner, one should then perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create obstacles to the *pravāraṇā*. In such a residence, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed with a single proclamation.
"Suppose that at the time of the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to point out faults) in a certain residence, many bhikṣus are ill.
The bhikṣus there think to themselves:
'The bhikṣus in this residence are ill; if we were to perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting it three times, the sick bhikṣus would be unable to endure prostrating themselves on their knees.'"
“If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā* by means of a single proclamation.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).

Having performed this, one should then perform the *pravāraṇā*; one must not create an obstacle to the *pravāraṇā*. In such a residence, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed by means of a single proclamation.
"For example, at a certain residence during the time of the *pravāraṇā*, it was raining lightly from the sky, covering the roof. The monks there thought to themselves:

'At this residence, the rain is falling lightly from the sky, covering the roof; if we perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting the three proclamations, the leaking roof will soil the monastic bedding and dampen the robes of the monks.'"
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā* by a single recitation.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Having performed this, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*; one should not create obstacles to the *pravāraṇā*. In such a residence, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed by a single recitation.
“Suppose, at the time of the *pravāraṇā* ceremony in a single residence, one or another of the eight calamities should arise:

whether it be the calamity of a king, the calamity of bandits, the calamity of fire, the calamity of water, the calamity of wild beasts, the calamity of crawling insects, the calamity of humans, or the calamity of non-humans.”
What is the difficulty of kings?

It is when a king, out of anger, issues a decree to arrest various śramaṇa sons of the Śākya, to beat, kill, bind, or drive them out; to seize their *kāṣāya* robes and give them to laypeople to wear; to compel them to serve as elephant troops, cavalry, chariot troops, infantry, or archers; to make them hold elephant hooks or leather reins; to make them carry palanquins in and out of military arrays; or to subject them to various miscellaneous corvée duties under individual officials.
The bhikṣus there reflected:
"In this residence, the king has issued a decree in anger to arrest the śramaṇa sons of the Śākyas.

They shall be killed, imprisoned, or driven out; their kāṣāyas shall be seized and given to laypeople to wear; they shall be made to serve as elephant troops, cavalry, chariot troops, infantry, or archers; they shall be made to hold elephant hooks or leather reins, carry palanquins in and out of military encampments, or perform various miscellaneous official duties. If we were to announce our *pravāraṇā* three times, our lives might be taken or our precepts broken."
“If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā* by means of a single proclamation.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
